item.title: Calabi-Bernstein type theorems for entire solutions of certain nonlinear elliptic equations in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.14319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide some extensions of the classical Calabi-Bernstein theorem to the case of entire solutions of certain nonlinear elliptic equations in two variables. Using an appropriate version of the Calabi correspondence, which formulates a duality between minimal graphs in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and maximal spacelike graphs in $\mathbb{L}^3$, our results are a consequence of recent Bernstein type results.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bildhauer, Martin Fuchs

item.title: The Liouville property for entire local minimizers from the space $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^2,\R^N)$ of variational integrals with linear growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.14321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider functions $u : \R^2 \rightarrow \R^N$ from the class $\Bloc$ which locally minimize the relaxed version of a variational integral with a strictly convex density being in addition of linear growth. It turns out that the boundedness of entire local minimizers $u$ implies their constancy.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bildhauer, Martin Fuchs

item.title: On Dolbeault's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.14359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb S^n$, $n\ge3$, for antipodally even functions and for axially symmetric functions whose critical density $|u|^{2n/(n-2)}$ has zero barycenter. In both cases, the Dirichlet coefficient improves by the optimal factor $2^{-2/n}$, while the coefficient of the $L^2$ term remains one. Equality holds precisely for constant functions. The even case resolves a conjecture of Dolbeault (2021).
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Wei, Zetian Yan, Zikai Ye

item.title: Uniqueness and stability of entropy waves among vanishing dissipation limits from the Navier--Stokes--Fourier System
item.description: arXiv:2610.14383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the stability of general entropy wave solutions of the compressible Euler equations (that is, profiles with constant velocity and pressure) in the class of vanishing dissipation limits from the Navier--Stokes--Fourier system. If the initial data of our sequence of solutions to the Navier--Stokes--Fourier system converges to the initial data of the entropy wave solution, we further have convergence of the solutions to the entropy wave. This gives uniqueness and stability of the entropy wave in this class. The proof is based on the $a$-contraction theory.
item.dc:creator: Cooper Faile, Ingrid Lacroix-Violet, Alexis F. Vasseur

item.title: Persistence of conormal analyticity for the Euler equations in the half-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.14408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the persistence of conormal analyticity through the $H^r$ norm, with $r \geq 4$, for the 3D incompressible Euler equations in the half-space $\Omega = \mathbb{R}_+^3$. We also establish a lower bound on the radius of conormal analyticity which depends on $\|u\|_{H^r}$ and initial data. In particular, persistence is established in both of the spaces $X_\tau^{\rm co}$ and $A_\tau^{\rm co}$, the former being based on the conormal operator $Z_k = \phi^k \partial_3^k$ and the latter being based on $L^k = (\phi \partial_3)^k$. Finally, we show that the norms $\|\cdot \|_{X_\tau^{\rm co}}$ and $\|\cdot \|_{A_\tau^{\rm co}}$ are equivalent up to a small loss in radius, the proof of which uses explicit identities relating the two conormal operators.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Ingimarson, Igor Kukavica, Marco Sammartino

item.title: Global existence and convergence of a density heat flow for strictly subcritical Liouville systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.14455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a density heat flow associated with normalized Liouville systems on a closed connected Riemannian surface, and we show that this flow leads to the existence of solutions for the corresponding subcritical Liouville systems. The coupling matrix is symmetric and entrywise nonnegative, with no invertibility, irreducibility or inverse-matrix sign assumption. Under the strict subcriticality conditions $8\pi\sum_{i\in J}\rho_i>\sum_{i,j\in J}a_{ij}\rho_i\rho_j$ for every nonempty set of components $J$, every smooth positive initial density of masses $\rho_i>0$ generates a unique global smooth positive solution converging in every $C^m$ norm to a stationary density. The limiting potentials solve the stationary Liouville system. Our proof uses entropy coercivity and a gradient inequality in the density variables, which also yields algebraic or exponential convergence rates.
item.dc:creator: Zetao Cheng, Haoyu Li, Woongbae Park, Lei Zhang

item.title: Domain dependence of Sobolev-curl constants and structure of critical curl-curl solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates intrinsic critical Sobolev-curl constants on bounded domains and the structure of finite-energy solutions to the critical curl-curl equation in R^3. First, for 1< p < 3, we prove that the intrinsic critical p-curl constant on (0, a)\times D is bounded above by a^{p/3} times a Sobolev quotient on D. The proof uses an aligned test field whose optimal curl-free correction vanishes. Consequently, these constants tend to zero along thin convex boxes. For p = 2, we construct explicit convex and nonconvex domains with intrinsic constant below the sharp scalar Sobolev constant. The nonconvex example gives an affirmative answer to the domain-existence question in Problem 5 of Mederski and Szulkin(Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 241 (2021), 1815-1842), while the convex example disproves the lower bound stated there for convex domains. Concerning their Problem 2, we obtain an implicit Newtonian representation of finite-energy solutions and exclude two special forms of solutions. These structural results do not yet provide an explicit ground state or an unconditional ground-state decay rate as asked in Problem 2.
item.dc:creator: Yong Liu, Jun Wang, Xuan Wang, Wen Yang

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Persistence of H2 Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Primitive Equations with Horizontal and Topography-Adapted Thermal Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.14555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the three-dimensional primitive equations with full viscosity and horizontal thermal diffusion in bounded domains. We establish global well-posedness for admissible $H^1$ initial data and persistence of $H^2$ regularity on the flat-bottom cylinder. The higher regularity analysis combines fractional hydrostatic Stokes regularity with anisotropic estimates of the vertical transport. We also consider variable-depth domains with positive $h\in C^3(\overline M)$ and a diffusion operator adapted to the topography compatible with layers $z/h(x,y)=\mathrm{constant}$. This operator reduces to $\Delta_H$ at constant depth and generally differs from the Cartesian horizontal Laplacian over a varying bottom. Its weighted formulation yields global strong solutions for admissible $H^1$ data. Persistence of $H^2$ regularity is proved under the additional assumption $\partial_\nu h=0$ on $\partial M$, where $\nu$ is the outward horizontal unit normal.
item.dc:creator: Qimin Wang, Mohammed Ziane

item.title: Spectral-Edge Continuation, Dimensional Crossover, and Endpoint Stability for Partially Confined Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the global geometry and endpoint dynamics of positive solutions of $-\Delta u+|y|^2u+\lambda u=g(u)$, $(y,z)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$, $m=N-d$. Despite the loss of coercivity at $\lambda=-d$, we construct a connected component of centered positive solutions with frequency projection $(-d,\infty)$, assuming subcritical asymptotics of $g$ at zero and infinity, a zero-mass Liouville condition, and a strict Hamiltonian sign condition. At the lower edge, $\lambda+d\rightarrow 0^+$, anisotropic rescaling selects the lowest confined harmonic mode coupled to an $m$-dimensional scalar ground state. As $\lambda\rightarrow\infty$, isotropic blow-up yields the $N$-dimensional scalar ground state, revealing a dimensional crossover. The endpoint profiles and mass laws hold for every sequence of centered positive solutions, not merely along this component. The proof combines Gaussian--exponential localization on compact frequency strips, Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction, compact spectral perturbation, and Leray--Schauder continuation. At both ends, we establish uniqueness and differentiability of the centered branch, identify the Morse indices and symmetry kernels of the real and imaginary linearizations in the full energy space, and derive sharp mass-slope asymptotics. Under standard Hamiltonian-flow hypotheses, the resulting slope criterion classifies orbital stability and instability away from the mass-critical powers. The mass map on this component, combined with endpoint control on the full centered solution set, yields existence, nonexistence, and multiplicity for normalized standing waves, revealing the roles of both critical exponents $2+4/m$ and $2+4/N$.
item.dc:creator: Xuexiu Zhong

item.title: The Strauss conjecture for the wave equation with critical damping
item.description: arXiv:2610.14610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Strauss conjecture concerns wave equations with power-type nonlinearities and seeks the optimal range of powers that admit global solutions for all sufficiently nice and sufficiently small initial data. In three spatial dimensions, it is well known that small data global existence is available provided that the power $p>p_c(3)=1+\sqrt{2}$, where $p_c(n)$ denotes the critical power in $n$-spatial dimensions. In the current article, the analogous problem is considered for damped wave equations where the damping coefficient is at the critical scaling. When $a$ denotes the constant multiple applied to the damping term, it is shown that the corresponding critical power is $p_c(3+a)$ provided that $a$ is sufficiently small.
item.dc:creator: Elliot Adamson, Jason Metcalfe, Chengbo Wang

item.title: The Strauss conjecture for the wave equation with scattering damping
item.description: arXiv:2610.14614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The focus of this article is to establish the existence portion of the Strauss conjecture for wave equations with spatially dependent scattering damping. In the current setting, the damping is not sufficiently strong to alter the critical Strauss exponent. In a subsequent study, the authors will consider the case of damping coefficients with critical decay where a shift of the Strauss exponent is expected. While several recent studies of the Strauss conjecture have relied upon weighted Strichartz estimates, here, instead, an approach that is based only on integrated local energy estimates, in particular those with both $r^p$ and ghost weights, is developed. This technique also applies to the problem for the free equation. Space-time Klainerman-Sobolev estimates provide the necessary decay to close the argument.
item.dc:creator: Elliot Adamson, Jason Metcalfe, Chengbo Wang

item.title: Liouville theorems for stable solutions to the mean curvature equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.14652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stable solutions of the mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =|u|^{p-1}u $$ in domains of $\mathbb R^n$. We establish Liouville-type results in three settings. First, for globally stable solutions in $\mathbb R^n$, we prove that $u\equiv0$ if $1<p<p_{JL}$, where $p_{JL}$ is the Joseph--Lundgren exponent. Second, for solutions in $\mathbb R^n$ that are stable outside a compact set, we show that if $n>2$ and $p=p_S$, where $p_S$ is the Sobolev critical exponent, then $u\equiv0$. Third, for solutions of the Dirichlet problem on connected unbounded domains with smooth boundary satisfying an epigraph-type geometric condition, we prove that if $n>2$, $1<p\le p_S$, and the solution is stable outside a compact set, then $u\equiv0$. The proofs are based on a gradient estimate for stable solutions, an integrability result, conservation laws and Pohozaev-type identities, and a unique continuation argument. These results extend Liouville-type theorems for stable solutions from the semilinear Lane--Emden equation to the mean curvature equation.
item.dc:creator: Fanheng Xu

item.title: Sharp decay estimates for subsolutions of fully nonlinear equations in thin domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.14667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reduce the problem of establishing pointwise upper decay estimates in thin domains for viscosity subsolutions of fully nonlinear partial differential equations to solving a one-dimensional differential inequality. The resulting estimates make explicit the interaction between the transverse geometry of the domain and the ellipticity of the equation, and are shown to be sharp. Our framework allows the ellipticity to degenerate at infinity and accommodates nonhomogeneous equations with lower-order terms. As an application, we obtain decay estimates for $p$-subharmonic functions when $1<p\leq 2$
item.dc:creator: John Fabricius, Niklas L. P. Lundstr\"om

item.title: Unique Determination of the Lam\'e Parameters in Three Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for static isotropic elasticity uniquely determines both smooth Lam\'e parameters in a bounded smooth domain of \(\mathbb R^3\) under strong convexity. The proof uses an exact four-component Laplace-type reduction, but its decisive identities are obtained from physical elastic solutions. The characteristic quotient of the reduced system has rank three, whereas the leading physical adjoint lift supplies only two directions. We construct the missing polarization from the first nonvanishing correction of a reduced amplitude in the kernel of that lift. Paired with fixed primal and adjoint quotient frames, the resulting complex geometrical optics solutions yield a complete family of holomorphically weighted \(3\times3\) matrix moments through the physical Betti identity. Cauchy--Plemelj factorization converts these moments into an invertible relative transport normalized in the common exterior. Holomorphic dependence on the projective null direction and transport rigidity then determine a material ratio and the shear modulus, hence both Lam\'e parameters. No smallness, symmetry, separability, or analyticity hypothesis is imposed.
item.dc:creator: Huaian Diao, Umidjon Durdiev

item.title: Nontrivial domains for the Bernoulli's overdetermined problem with small constant vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2610.14742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first apply the implicit function theorem to find nontrivial solutions to the following Bernoulli's overdetermined problem \begin{equation} -\Delta u=\gamma\,\, \text{in}\,\,\Omega \setminus\overline{D}, \,\, u=1,\,\,\partial_\mathbf{n} u=Q\,\,\text{on}\,\,\partial D, \,\,u=0\,\,\text{on}\,\,\partial\Omega \nonumber \end{equation} for a fixed boundary $\partial\Omega$ and a free boundary $\partial D$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ with $N\geq2$, where $\gamma$ is a sufficiently small constant, the Bernoulli value $Q$ is determined by the construction, and $\Omega \setminus\overline{D}$ is a bounded ring-shaped domain. In dimension $N=n+1$ with $n\geq2$, we further study the existence of a nontrivial unbounded domain $\Omega \setminus\overline{D}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ such that the Bernoulli's overdetermined problem admits a solution. This unbounded domain we construct is periodic in one variable and radial in the other variables by bifurcation analysis.
item.dc:creator: Yong Zhang, Jialong Zhu

item.title: Generic nondegeneracy of constant mean curvature radial graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.14755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a smooth domain $D\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$, $N\geq 3$, and a positive constant $H$, we study radial graphs over $D$ with constant mean curvature $H$ which meet orthogonally the boundary of the cone spanned by $D$. The corresponding problem is given by a quasilinear elliptic equation on $D$ with homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. We investigate the structure of the solution set under smooth perturbations of the domain which are parametrized by an open set of $C^{3,\alpha}$-diffeomorphisms of the sphere. After pulling the equation back to a fixed reference domain, we apply a classical transversality theorem and prove that, in the class of domains for which $N-1$ does not belong to the Neumann spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, there is a residual set for which every solution is nondegenerate. A consequence of our result is that, for every such domain and every $R>0$, the set of solutions whose $C^{2,\alpha}$-norm is bounded by $R$ is finite.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Iacopetti, Filomena Pacella

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
item.description:
arXiv:2610.14786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schr"odinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc
eq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. In the parameter regime $e
eq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. This result does not require the non-resonance condition appearing in Takaoka's periodic theory, while the condition $e
eq0$ naturally arises in the modulation setting considered here. Finally, motivated by the long-time regime relevant for modulation, we establish uniform long-time control without imposing a smallness assumption on the initial datum. Using the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow, we obtain uniform $H^s$ bounds on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for integer $s\ge2$. For non-integer real $s\ge2$, the maximal $H^s$ solution exists on the same time scale, while uniform control is obtained at a lower regularity, with a loss of less than one derivative.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Belloni, Filippo Giuliani

item.title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part I: Blow-up Analysis and Compactness
item.description: arXiv:2610.14797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a priori estimates and compactness results for positive solutions of the CR Nirenberg problem under natural weighted flatness conditions. The proofs combine refined blow-up analysis, Pohozaev identities, and the complete classification of positive entire solutions to the critical CR Yamabe equation recently obtained by Li--Liu--Ma \cite{LLM2026} and Li \cite{L2026}. Existence and degree results are established in our subsequent paper \cite{QTWPartII}.
item.dc:creator: Jiechen Qiang, Zhongwei Tang, Heming Wang

item.title: Uniqueness and stability for inverse potential scattering with multiple wavenumbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.14978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with the inverse scattering problem of determining a real-valued potential for the three-dimensional Schr\"odinger equation from multi-wavenumber data. Under suitable a priori bounds, we establish local increasing stability from near-field Dirichlet data on a fixed sphere for polynomially decaying potentials, and global increasing stability from full far-field amplitudes for exponentially decaying potentials. The stability estimates consist of a noise term and a remainder term, with the latter decreasing as the upper measured wavenumber increases. We also obtain global uniqueness from exact near-field data under weaker regularity assumptions. The analysis combines analytic continuation, weighted resolvent estimates, and half-ray identities whose differences at chord endpoints cancel the unknown exterior contribution.
item.dc:creator: Dong Qiu, Xiang Xu, Yue Zhao

item.title: Stability in the determination of the coefficients for coupled relativistic Schr\"odinger system
item.description: arXiv:2610.15013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we prove a stability result for the identification of the coefficients appearing in a coupled relativistic Schr\"odinger system posed on a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^{1+n}$, where $n \geq 3$. More precisely, by utilizing input-output operator, where Neumann boundary data are available only on a subset of the boundary, and constructing an appropriate geometric optics solution, we derive a stability estimate of $\log$-$\log$ type for the matrix-valued first-order coefficients. This result is subsequently used to obtain a $\log$-$\log$-$\log$ type stability estimate for the zeroth-order matrix-valued potential.
item.dc:creator: Nitesh Kumar, Parveen Kumar, Tanmay Sarkar

item.title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee

item.title: Single-Measurement H\"older Stability for a Spatial Coefficient in a Wave Equation with Principal Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.15045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recovery of a spatial coefficient in the principal memory flux of a three-dimensional wave equation with the prescribed exponential relaxation kernel $\beta e^{-\beta t}$, where $\beta>0$ is known. From a single finite-time lateral Cauchy measurement generated by one fixed, coefficient-independent initial displacement that is affine near the unknown region, with zero initial velocity, we establish global uniqueness and conditional $L^2$-H\"older stability. Two difficulties arise in this setting. The affine initial displacement makes the initial acceleration vanish in the unknown region, while the coefficient-difference equation contains a divergence-form source whose direct $L^2$ estimate loses a spatial derivative. We establish an acoustic Carleman estimate that controls the vector source and its time derivative without spatially differentiating the source. The affine condition identifies the relevant initial trace with a directional derivative of the coefficient difference, and the quadratic temporal vanishing of the source permits absorption in the weighted estimate. A transport estimate then yields stability uniformly over a bounded, uniformly coercive $W^{5,\infty}$ coefficient class, without an ordering condition or a smallness assumption near a reference coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Huaian Diao, Umidjon Durdiev

item.title: Exact $L^2$-growth profiles for the free wave equation: Sharp constants, critical regularity, and local energy decay
item.description: arXiv:2610.15086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the large-time behavior of the $L^2$-norm of solutions to the free wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^N$ and, more generally, their homogeneous Sobolev norms of negative order. We refine and extend the results of R. Ikehata [J. Hyperbolic Differ. Equ. 20 (2023)] who identified and quantified the infinite-time $L^2$-growth of free waves in dimensions $N=1,2$. For finite-energy data with $u_1\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, we derive exact first-order asymptotics: when $P=\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}u_1(x)\,dx\neq0$, the squared $L^2$-norm grows linearly for $N=1$ and logarithmically for $N=2$, with a leading coefficient depending only on $P$. In particular, no weighted moment assumption on $u_1$ is required; $u_1\in L^1\cap L^2$ suffices. More generally, we prove that the $L^2$-norm is bounded, and hence convergent, if and only if $u_1\in\dot H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. We further establish first-order asymptotic profiles in negative-order homogeneous Sobolev spaces, covering polynomial growth, logarithmic growth, and convergence to a finite limit according to the Sobolev index. These results reveal a unified low-frequency mechanism underlying the low-dimensional $L^2$-growth. We also derive second-order asymptotic expansions in dimension one and at the critical Sobolev index in dimensions $N\ge2$. Finally, in dimension two, the exact $L^2$-asymptotics yield a sharper local energy decay estimate with an explicit upper asymptotic constant independent of the localization radius.
item.dc:creator: Vishvesh Kumar, Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: Plane wave representation for wave scattering on a sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.15121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.
item.dc:creator: Valentin D. Kunz, Andrey V. Shanin, Raphael C. Assier

item.title: Double-arc rearrangement and the symmetric isoperimetric problem in Gauss space
item.description: arXiv:2610.15133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a new rearrangement in Gauss space transforming symmetric sets while decreasing their Gaussian perimeter. We use this rearrangement to analyze the minimizers of the Gaussian perimeter among symmetric sets.
item.dc:creator: Marco Barchiesi, Filippo Cagnetti, Vesa Julin

item.title: Extremals for singular Onofri type inequality in weighted Sobolev spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.15195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $N$-dimensional Euclidean Onofri inequality was proved by Del Pino and Dolbeault for smooth compactly supported functions in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N \ge 2$. In this paper, we consider the singular version introduced by Lam and Lu, and extend it to a natural weighted Sobolev space. Next, we establish a sharp singular Carleson-Chang type inequality and prove its equivalence with the singular $N$-dimensional Euclidean Onofri inequality. Furthermore, we prove the existence of nontrivial, non-constant optimizers for the functional associated with the singular Euclidean Onofri inequality, answering open questions left by Del Pino and Dolbeault in the non-singular case, and by Lam and Lu in the case with singularities. To this end, we exploit the classification result obtained for a singular Liouville-type equation involving the $N$-Laplacian. We also prove the conformal invariance of the functional, establish the sharpness of the singular $N$-dimensional Euclidean Onofri inequality in terms of optimal constants, and state several consequences, including a sharp Poincar\'e inequality.
item.dc:creator: Natalino Borgia, Silvia Cingolani, Rub\'en Fi\~nana Aranega, Gabriele Mancini

item.title: Polynomial mixing for infinite-energy solutions of the white-forced Navier--Stokes equation in an infinite pipe
item.description: arXiv:2610.15216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the infinite-energy solutions to the white-forced Navier--Stokes equation in an infinite pipe $\mathbb{R}\times (-1,1)$ with no-slip boundary conditions. The equation is globally well-posed in uniformly local spaces satisfying the divergence-free condition. Under suitable degeneracy and spatial decay assumptions on the noise, we prove the uniqueness of the invariant measure and establish polynomial mixing in the dual-Lipschitz metric. This provides an affirmative answer to Open Problem 1 posed by Kuksin and Shirikyan \cite{KS17} in the case of zero cross-sectional flux.
item.dc:creator: Meng Zhao

item.title: Uniqueness of Bound States for Double-Power Scalar Field Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the uniqueness of bound states for the following scalar field equation $$ -\Delta u+u=-\varepsilon |u|^{q-1}u+|u|^{p-1}u \,\ \ \mbox{in}\,\ \mathbb R^N, \,\ \varepsilon>0,\tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $ N\ge3,\ 1<p<(N+2)/(N-2)$ and $q>1$ satisfies $q \neq p$. For each integer $k \geq 1$, we prove that the equation $(*)$ has, up to translation and reflection, a unique bound state with precisely $k$ nodes in a natural coupling regime, where $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small. Our results address a conjecture of [H. Berestycki and P. L. Lions, ARMA, 1983][M. X. Tang, Invent. Math., 2026] on the uniqueness of fixed-node bound states for the equation $(*)$.
item.dc:creator: Yujin Guo, Wei Ji, Yong Luo

item.title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to Lane--Emden Equations on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.15275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stable solutions of the Lane--Emden equation $$-\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$$ on graphs with polynomial volume growth. Due to the lack of a chain rule in the discrete setting, we establish suitable algebraic inequalities which serve as substitutes for the usual differential identities. Combining these inequalities with the stability condition and cutoff arguments, we obtain nonexistence results for stable solutions in a range of exponents analogous to the Joseph--Lundgren range. As an application, we derive a lower bound for the Sobolev best constant in the discrete setting.
item.dc:creator: Weiqi Guan

item.title: Global solutions to the fully nonlinear obstacle problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.15313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate global solutions to the fully nonlinear obstacle problem. We prove that, after factoring out invariant directions, the coincidence set of any global solution belongs to one of the following four types: a single point, a compact convex set with nonempty interior, a ray for $n=1$, or a slender body for $n\geq 2$, where $n$ denotes the spatial dimension. Furthermore, we establish a bijection between the collection of all global solutions with compact coincidence sets and a family of functions describing the asymptotic behavior of such solutions at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Yi Cao, Dongsheng Li

item.title: pper and Lower Bounds for Blow-up Times in Coupled Reaction--Diffusion Systems with Nonlocal Sources
item.description: arXiv:2610.15367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the following reaction-diffusion system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_t=\Delta u+F\bigl(x,t,u,v,V(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\Om\times(0,T), v_t=\Delta v+G\bigl(x,t,u,v,U(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\Om\times(0,T), \mathcal B u=\mathcal B v=0, & (x,t)\in\partial\Om\times(0,T), u(x,0)=u_0(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_0(x), & x\in\Om, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where \begin{equation*} U(t)=\int_{\Om}u(x,t)\dd x,\qquad V(t)=\int_{\Om}v(x,t)\dd x, \end{equation*} and the boundary operator $\mathcal B$ is either \[ \mathcal B_D w=w \qquad\text{or}\qquad \mathcal B_N w=\partial_\nu w, \] $\Om\subset\R^N$ be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary, $N\ge 1$, and $\nu$ is the outward unit normal on $\partial\Om$. Under certain conditions, we obtain the upper and lower bounds for the blowup time of the solution to the system.
item.dc:creator: Xin Zhao, Aynuer Ailatusi, Xianfa Song, Zeen Song

item.title: Uniqueness of prescribed-node radial bound states for a zero-mass double-power equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study radial bound states of \[ \Delta u-\abs{u}^{q-1}u+\abs{u}^{p-1}u=0 \quad\text{in }\R^n, \qquad n\ge3,\qquad 1<q<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}. \] For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that there is exactly one radial bound state with $k$ simple zeros and $u(0)>0$. Its absolute maximum is attained at the origin. This confirms the zero-mass, Sobolev-subcritical case of Tang's double-power uniqueness conjecture. The proof adapts Tang's phase-transition analysis and combines it with a finite-level separation argument inspired by Cort\'azar--Garc\'ia-Huidobro--Yarur. Three main difficulties arise in the zero-mass double-power setting: the sign changes of key comparison quantities in the low-amplitude region, the possible failure of pointwise positivity of an auxiliary quantity when $n=3$ and $p+q<3$, and the absence of exponential decay at infinity. We overcome these difficulties by introducing bridge functionals to propagate the required sign information through low amplitudes, establishing a weighted integral positivity estimate in the exceptional three-dimensional range, and combining a radial-flux tail estimate with finite-level inverse-branch comparison. We also establish the strict ordering of the bound-state shooting heights and show that the shooting variation along the \(k\)-node state has exactly \(k+1\) simple zeros.
item.dc:creator: Wenjing Chen, Zexi Wang

item.title: Spectral G\aa rding Elliptic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spectral G\aa rding elliptic equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal G\aa rding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Sz\'ekelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact K\"ahler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal G\aa rding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Hao Fang, Biao Ma

item.title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give new, elementary proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation and the constant quadratic Hessian equation, based on the two-point maximum principle. The arguments require only one differentiation of the equation. For the Monge-Amp\`ere equation, the inhomogeneous term is assumed to be positive and continuously differentiable. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Jui-Yun Hung, Jiakun Liu, Neil Trudinger

item.title: Classification of minimal-mass blowup solutions to the mass-critical Hartree equation at the $L^2$-critical level
item.description: arXiv:2610.15460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the focusing mass-critical Hartree equation \[ iu_t+\Delta u=-\bigl(|x|^{-2}*|u|^2\bigr)u \] at the ground-state mass $M(Q)$. We prove that, up to the symmetries of the equation, every global minimal-mass non-scattering solution is a solitary wave, while every finite-time minimal-mass blowup solution is a pseudo-conformal image of a solitary wave. This extends the results of \cite{LZ28,Miao-Xu-Zhao3,Wang-Gao} to the scaling-critical space $L^2$ and removes the radial assumption in the global case.
item.dc:creator: Zuyu Ma, Changxing Miao, Jiqiang Zheng

item.title: Boundary Vanishing Orders and Asymptotic Expansions for Planar Harmonic Functions with a Sublinear Robin Condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.15465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study boundary vanishing orders and asymptotic expansions of planar harmonic functions satisfying the sublinear Robin condition $\partial_\nu u=\lambda u-|u|^{p-1}u,$ with $\lambda\geq0$ and $0<p<1$. For nontrivial global solutions on bounded connected Lipschitz domains, we bound the number of nodal domains by the number of Steklov eigenvalues strictly below $\lambda$ and establish finite vanishing order at every boundary point. The boundary scaling gives the critical exponent $\frac{1}{1-p}$. On $C^1$ boundaries, every positive subcritical vanishing order is an integer, and the leading term is a unique homogeneous Neumann profile in conformal coordinates. At a noninteger critical order, the rescaled solution converges in normalized graph coordinates to an explicit homogeneous profile determined by $p$ up to sign. Every supercritical bulk vanishing order $m$ is an integer, with a unique homogeneous Dirichlet profile in conformal coordinates. The boundary trace has vanishing order $\frac{m-1}{p}>m$. Integer critical vanishing orders are excluded if the boundary is $C^1$ with Dini mean oscillation.
item.dc:creator: Hairong Liu, Long Tian, Xiaoping Yang

item.title: Orbital stability of solitary wave solutions of the derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in the endpoint case
item.description: arXiv:2610.15507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the orbital stability of solitary waves for the derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation $$iq_t+q_{xx}+i\partial_x\bigl(|q|^2q\bigr)=0, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}.$$ For the endpoint solitary waves satisfying $c>0$ and $c^2=4\omega$, we prove the orbital stability in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ without any additional assumptions. The proof uses conservation of mass and the second Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}_2$ to keep the B\"acklund-transformed solution small in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ uniformly in time. We establish an inverse B\"acklund compactness result to reconstruct the algebraic solitary wave as the spectral zero approaches the negative real axis.
item.dc:creator: Jia Shen, Yifei Wu, Changping Yang

item.title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.15511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.
item.dc:creator: Daniele De Gennaro, Salvatore Stuvard

item.title: A Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlinear Damping and Supercritical Variable-Exponent Logarithmic Sources
item.description: arXiv:2610.15528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a viscoelastic wave equation with nonlinear variable-exponent damping and a variable-exponent logarithmic source, allowing supercritical growth. The main difficulties arise from the failure of the source to map the energy space into $L^2(\Omega)$, the sign-changing logarithmic potential, and the lack of Sobolev control of the displacement for supercritical damping. Under an exponent condition linking the source and damping exponents, we prove local existence, an energy identity, and a continuation criterion. We prove finite-time blow-up for nontrivial solutions with nonpositive shifted initial energy. We also establish a blow-up criterion based on a sufficiently large initial displacement--velocity pairing, with a threshold depending on the positive part of the shifted initial energy, and derive an explicit upper bound for the lifespan. This criterion allows us to construct blow-up data at every prescribed level of the original energy. For initial data in a suitable stable region, solutions exist globally. For damping within the Sobolev range, a general relaxation condition yields energy decay estimates that include exponential and polynomial rates. Beyond this range, a time-weighted displacement estimate and a splitting of the memory integral give logarithmic decay.
item.dc:creator: Menglan Liao, Mingxue Zhang

item.title: Homogenization of an optimal control problem for a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a 3D perforated domain
item.description: arXiv:2610.15584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the homogenization of an optimal control problem governed by a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a periodically perforated three-dimensional domain. The obstacles are Lipschitz sets of size $\varepsilon^\alpha$, $\alpha>3$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period. The fluid satisfies the no-slip condition on the outer boundary and the free-slip condition on the obstacles, the phase-field equation contains a source term, and the convective term carries a pore-scale Reynolds number that tends to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$. The control is a distributed body force, and the cost functional tracks the velocity in $L^2$ and the order parameter in $H^1$. Since uniqueness of weak solutions of the state system is not known for fixed $\varepsilon$, the control-to-state relation is multivalued, and we pose the microscopic problems over control-state pairs. We prove the existence of microscopic optimal pairs and the sequential $\Gamma$-convergence of the cost functionals to the cost functional of a control problem governed by the unsteady Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system on the full domain. As a consequence, the optimal values converge, every cluster point of microscopic optimal pairs is optimal for the homogenized problem, and the optimal controls converge strongly along the corresponding subsequences. The $\liminf$ inequality follows from the homogenization of the state system, including the strong convergence of the gradients of the order parameter. Only the recovery sequence requires uniqueness of weak solutions of the homogenized system, which we prove when the outer boundary is of class $C^{2,1}$.
item.dc:creator: Amartya Chakrabortty, Haradhan Dutta, Hari Shankar Mahato

item.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the half-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.15588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy that accounts for the electric boundary contribution through the Helmholtz projection. We also prove algebraic decay under an additional low-frequency assumption on the initial data. If the density perturbation, velocity and electric field have finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, where $1/2\leq s<1$, then the solution decays at the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$ in the full energy norm. The decay estimate follows from the formulation in terms of the momentum $\rho u$, uniform negative-order estimates and interpolation with the dissipation.
item.dc:creator: Hairong Liu, Jinlong Wu, Hua Zhong

item.title: Negative Sobolev regularity and optimal decay for the fractional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system
item.description: arXiv:2610.15594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem in $\R^{3}$ for the repulsive compressible Navier-Stokes-Riesz system with Riesz exponent $0<s<1$ and viscosity $0<\varepsilon\leq1$, where the Riesz interaction $\nabla(-\Delta)^{-s}(\rho-\bar{\rho})$ is a generalization of the Coulomb interaction for electrons. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium, with the solenoidal component of the initial velocity of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions. We derive time-decay estimates in $L^{2}$ norms and $L^{\infty}$ norms that capture both uniform-in-$\varepsilon$ dispersive behavior and viscosity-dependent dissipation. We further establish a global-in-time inviscid limit to the irrotational global solution of the compressible Euler-Riesz system whose initial data consist of the same density and the curl-free component of the velocity, with an explicit convergence rate in $W^{k,p}$ norms. The proof combines viscosity-adapted dispersive estimates, normal-form analysis and nonlinear energy estimates with control of both negative and positive Sobolev norms.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xu, Junhao Zhang

item.title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part II: Existence and Topological Degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.15597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a continuation of Part~I \cite{QTWPartI}, where blow-up analysis and compactness results for the CR Nirenberg problem were established. We prove some existence and degree results for the CR Nirenberg problem on the standard sphere. More precisely, we first prove existence results under antipodal and, more generally, finite-group symmetries. Without symmetry, we derive a Leray--Schauder degree formula under natural flatness conditions, yielding existence results for positive prescribed curvatures with certain homogeneous expansions at critical points. We also obtain Aubin-type inequalities under a vanishing first-moment condition, uniformly near the critical exponent.
item.dc:creator: Jiechen Qiang, Zhongwei Tang, Heming Wang

item.title: Blow-down and immediate onset of positivity in the Neumann problem for (super-)fast diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the degenerate parabolic equation $u_t=\nabla\cdot (u^{m-1}\nabla u)$, the homogeneous Neumann problem in smoothly bounded domains $\Omega\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ is considered in the (super-fast) diffusion range when $m\in (-\infty,1)$. Upper and lower estimates for solutions are inferred by means of two Moser-type iterations, and optimality properties of these bounds are derived using comparison arguments. On the basis of the accordingly obtained information on regularization into spaces of bounded and uniformly positive functions, a result on global solvability in an associated initial-boundary value problem is achieved for all nonnegative and nontrivial initial data belonging to $L^1(\Omega) \cap \bigcup_{s>n(1-m)/2} L^s(\Omega)$.
item.dc:creator: Youshan Tao (School of Mathematical Sciences, CMA-Shanghai, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, P.R.China)

item.title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part I. Monge--Amp\`ere case
item.description: arXiv:2610.15693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study positive $(n-1)$-convex entire subsolutions of the normalized real $(n-1)$ Monge--Amp\`ere equation $\operatorname{det}^{\frac1n}\bigl(\Delta uI-D^2u\bigr)=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ in $\mathbb R^n$. Under two sets of structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2-\frac1n$. Our results cover the pure-gradient degenerate case $f\equiv0$ with $0<q<1$, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and the case where $g$ changes sign. For $q=2-\frac1n$, we recover the Keller--Osserman condition for the gradient-independent equation, prove nonexistence when $g$ is eventually positive, and obtain an exponentially weighted condition when $g$ has a nonpositive limit at infinity. This is the first of two companion papers and treats the determinant case.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Ji, Feida Jiang, Mengni Li

item.title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part II. $k$-Hessian case
item.description: arXiv:2610.15697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study admissible entire subsolutions and radial boundary blow-up solutions of $S_k^{\frac1k}[\Delta uI-D^2u]=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ for $1\leq k<n$, continuing our study of the determinant case $k=n$ in Part I. Under structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2$. Our results cover the non-Lipschitz case $0<q<1$ with a possibly vanishing zero-order term, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and sign-changing gradient coefficients. We also characterize finite-radius blow-up of radial solutions and derive two-sided estimates for the blow-up radius, as well as pointwise upper bounds for their profiles in terms of inverse Keller--Osserman functions.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Ji, Feida Jiang, Mengni Li

item.title: Small-speed solitary-wave stability and global well-posedness for a Bessel-regularized Airy equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove orbital stability of minimizing solitary waves at sufficiently small positive speeds for an Airy equation with a quadratic interaction filtered by a Bessel potential of order one. The stability hypotheses are verified: constrained minimization gives one negative direction, the small-speed KdV limit and operator-norm perturbation of the profile resolvent give a one-dimensional translation kernel, and a differentiable rescaled branch with uniformly bounded derivative gives a positive slope of the quadratic invariant. A conserved Lyapunov functional then proves orbital stability in the three-halves-derivative energy space and the perturbation also gives uniqueness of centered minimizers at small speed. The dynamical framework is supplied by a direct Bourgain-space bilinear estimate, local well-posedness in the square-integrable class, unconditional uniqueness from one-quarter derivative onward, and global well-posedness in the half-derivative energy space. For every prescribed positive speed, constrained minimization constructs smooth positive profiles that are symmetric, strictly monotone away from their center, and exponentially localized. At general positive speeds the stability criterion remains conditional on nondegeneracy and the slope condition.
item.dc:creator: Germ\'an Preciado L\'opez

item.title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular boundaries of dimension close to $1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $0<s<1$ we construct a compact $s$-Ahlfors regular set $K\subset\mathbb C$ for which harmonic measure of $\mathbb C\setminus K$ with pole at infinity is comparable to $\mathcal H^s|_K$. In particular, there is no dimension drop for any dimension $s<1$. The construction is $N$-adic and based on configurations close to the $N$-th roots of unity. We adjust the positions of the children by small polynomial deformations so that the logarithmic potential of the natural Bernoulli measure becomes constant in the limit. A first-mode correction gives the range $s<2/3$, while corrections of arbitrary finite order yield the full range $0<s<1$.
item.dc:creator: Yingying Cai, Cole Jeznach, Xavier Tolsa

item.title: Explicit counterexamples to Frank-Loss optimizer conjectures for critical Dirac and vector Sobolev inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.15787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frank and Loss proposed critical Sobolev inequalities for the Dirac operator and for vector fields. They conjectured optimality of their spinorial family and wrote that it is conceivable that the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau potential is an optimizer. Wang and Zhang recently disproved both optimizer claims using direct comparison and instability arguments. We compute closed-form quotients for two elementary families of explicit competitors with strictly smaller quotients. For every $d\geq2$, the spinorial competitor is a constant spinor multiplied by a scalar Aubin-Talenti optimizer. For every $d\geq3$, the vector competitor is the planar azimuthal field \[ A_d(x)=\frac{d}{(1+\lvert x\rvert^2)^2} (-x_2,x_1,0,\ldots,0). \] It lies in the nonlinear gauge and its quotient is computed in closed form. For every odd $d\geq3$, it gives an explicit proof of nonoptimality of the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau-Dunne-Min potential. In dimension three, this field is a specific member of the competitor family of Wang and Zhang: it is a linear combination of the Loss-Yau potential and its reflected twin. Its axisymmetry gives a negative answer to their question about minimization within the $\mathrm{SO}(2)\times 1$-invariant class.
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Bieganowski, Jaros{\l}aw Mederski

item.title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular flat boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.15805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an $N$-adic modification of the construction of David-Jeznach-Julia for compact subsets of the real line $\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ for which harmonic measure for the complementary domains has no dimension drop. In particular, we show that for every $s\in(0,1/2)$, there exists an $s$-Ahlfors regular compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that $\mathrm{dim}\omega^\infty=s$, where $\omega^\infty$ denotes harmonic measure for $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with pole at infinity. Combined with a result of the third author, this shows that the threshold $1/2$ is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Yingying Cai, Cole Jeznach, Xavier Tolsa

item.title: Regularity for Minimizers of Mixed-Smoothness Variational Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.15844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the first partial regularity results for minimizers of a class of suitably quasiconvex variational integrals defined on anisotropic Sobolev spaces. These variational integrals are related to higher gradient continuum models for pantographic metamaterials.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristensen, Adam Prosinski, Aidan Strong

item.title: Lack of exponential stability for thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we prove that the classical thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with thermal coupling acting only on the bending moment are not exponentially stable under full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions if the equal wave speed condition is not satisfied. Combined with their well-known converses, our results provide complete characterizations of exponential stability in terms of the coefficients of each system. To the best of our knowledge, these characterizations were previously known only under mixed boundary conditions. The proof is based on the introduction of a boundary correction term in the standard trigonometric ansatz so that the full homogeneous Dirichlet conditions are satisfied.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Roberto de Lima

item.title: Sharp stability for mixed bubbles on hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.15920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp residual stability estimates for the critical Poincar\'e-Sobolev equation near sums of one positive hyperbolic solution and one projected Euclidean bubble in dimensions at least four. The estimates are uniform in the relative positions of the centers. The sharp rate is linear except in dimension six, where it contains a square root of a logarithm. For nonnegative functions, the same estimates hold under an energy constraint near the sum of the two profile energies for \(\lambda\) outside a finite set, and an additional mass constraint removes this restriction. For arbitrary finite numbers of profiles, we identify and realize all nonnegative Palais-Smale levels. We characterize the parameters at which different pairs of profile numbers have the same energy and show that the limiting energy and mass determine both profile numbers.
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Wei, Zetian Yan, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Regularity theorems for Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system
item.description: arXiv:2610.15952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove several regularity theorems concerning Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system. The main lemma (i.e. ``Decoupling Lemma") says that the component functions of such solutions satisfy the homogeneous Pucci inequalities. This allows us to apply the regularity theory for scalar viscosity solutions for elliptic PDE component-wise to a viscosity solution for the system. As a result of the Decoupling Lemma, we deduce that 2D Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the system are analytic in the interior, and obtain a quantitative partial regularity theorem. We also prove a geometric Harnack inequality for Lipschitz solutions. The Harnack inequality yields a strong maximum principle and half-space Liouville theorem. Another significant consequence of the lemma is a boundary regularity theorem for Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Notably, our theorem does not require any density assumption at the graph boundary, and we do not assume stationarity. This is used to prove a classification theorem for the singular set of a 4D stationary solution on a bounded domain. We also prove an $\varepsilon$-regularity theorem extending a result of the author. To conclude, we survey open problems. As an example, we have included a Bernstein-type theorem for 3D homogeneous entire Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Taken together, our results suggest that viscosity methods are a useful tool for studying the regularity of minimal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Dimler

item.title: Global stability and sharp decay for the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations without thermal diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.16029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with positive horizontal and vertical viscosity and without thermal diffusion. Our main results are fourfold. First, for every integer \(s\ge4\), we prove that sufficiently small, compatible, doubly periodic \(H^s\) perturbations of a stably stratified rest state with an affine temperature profile generate unique global strong solutions; the horizontal velocity and temperature remain uniformly small at the initial Sobolev order despite the derivative loss in the full diagnostic vertical velocity, and strict stratification persists. Second, we establish an inverse-map conservation law that determines the terminal temperature solely from the initial temperature: the terminal label is identified as the normalized increasing rearrangement of the initial label modulo the vertical period, and the terminal perturbation admits a quadratic expansion with cubic remainder. Third, the limiting equilibrium uniquely minimizes the quadratic perturbation energy among compatible, strictly stratified states with the same periodic label distribution. Finally, we establish sharp algebraic decay in suitable lower-order Sobolev norms for both velocity components and for the temperature and pressure differences from equilibrium. Exact nonlinear solutions provide matching lower bounds, establishing optimality for uniform estimates over the small-data class. The proofs combine weighted energy methods, spectral analysis, and inverse-map identities.
item.dc:creator: Fengjie Luo, Quan Wang

item.title: Boundary regularity for fractional porous medium-type equations in bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.16113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove boundary H\"older regularity for fractional porous medium-type equations in bounded smooth domains with zero exterior data. For $0<\sigma<1$, $n>2\sigma$, and $m>1$, we show that nonnegative weak dual solutions $v$ of $\partial_t v+(-\Delta)^\sigma(v^m)=0$ satisfy \[ \frac{v}{d^{\sigma/m}}\in C_{x,t}^{\alpha,\frac{\alpha m}{\sigma(m+1)}} \] up to the boundary and away from the initial time, for some $\alpha\in(0,\sigma)$, where $d$ denotes the distance to the boundary. More generally, we establish boundary H\"older estimates for $u/d^\sigma$ for nonnegative viscosity solutions of $\partial_t u=u^\gamma Lu$, with $0<\gamma<1$ and initial data comparable to $d^\sigma$. Here $L$ is a symmetric stable operator of order $2\sigma$ whose measurable angular density is bounded above and below by positive constants. Our proof combines comparison principles and boundary barriers with a blow-up and compactness argument based on a Liouville theorem for ancient solutions in a half-space.
item.dc:creator: Mengyu Huo, Tianling Jin, Jingang Xiong

item.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.
item.dc:creator: Xing Wang, Cheng Zhang

item.title: A counterexample to integral Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci estimates for a nonlocal operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.16162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a counterexample to integral Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci estimates for nonlocal inequalities of the form \begin{equation*} L_au(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\delta_yu(x) \frac{a(x,y)}{|y|^{n+\sigma}}\,dy \ge-f(x)\quad\text{in }B_1, \end{equation*} with $u\le0$ in $\mathbb R^n\setminus B_1$, where $\delta_yu(x)=u(x+y)+u(x-y)-2u(x)$, and the measurable coefficient satisfies \begin{equation}\tag{C} \lambda\le a(x,y)\le\Lambda,\qquad a(x,y)=a(x,-y),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n,\quad y\ne0. \end{equation} More precisely, for every $n\ge1$, $0<\sigma<2$, and $0<\lambda<\Lambda$, there exist a fixed coefficient $a(x,y)$ satisfying \textup{(C)}, a constant $d>0$, and nonnegative functions $u_j,f_j\in C_c^\infty(B_1)$ such that $L_au_j\ge-f_j$ in $B_1$, $0\le f_j\le1$, and $|\operatorname{supp}f_j|\to0$ as $j\to\infty$, while $u_j\ge d$ on $B_{1/4}$ for every $j$. Consequently, this fixed operator admits no $L^p$ maximum estimate for any $1\le p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Jiang, Lei Xu

item.title: C^(sigma+alpha) regularity for fractional Hamilton-Jacobi equations, and rates of convergence in periodic homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2610.16211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two related questions for nonlocal equations of Bellman type: the regularity of solutions when the set of controls depends on the state variable, and the periodic homogenization of stationary nonlocal Hamilton-Jacobi equations driven by uniformly elliptic integro-differential operators of order $\sigma\in(0,2)$, whose kernels depend simultaneously on the slow variable, the fast periodic variable and the control. The effective equation is again a nonlocal Bellman equation, but its supremum runs over a set of viscosity Mather measures that varies with the space variable, in a merely H\"older continuous way. We first develop a $C^{\sigma+\alpha}$ regularity theory for nonlocal Bellman equations with H\"older continuous, state-dependent index sets, extending the Schauder estimates of Caffarelli-Silvestre and Serra, in a general framework independent of homogenization. We then use these estimates as a source of compactness to construct a classical solution of the effective problem, unique among bounded classical solutions. Finally, combining this regularity with discounted approximate correctors, we make the perturbed test function method quantitative, and prove that the whole family of solutions converges to the effective solution, with the explicit rate $\epsilon^{\sigma\alpha/(2+\alpha)}$, where $\alpha$ is the H\"older exponent of the data.
item.dc:creator: Adina Ciomaga, Andrei Rodriguez-Paredes, Erwin Topp

item.title: Sharp decay characterization for the Oldroyd-B system with only velocity dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the incompressible Oldroyd-B system on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, in the regime in which the velocity is the only dissipated quantity: the stress tensor undergoes neither relaxation nor diffusion. In this regime the operator $\mathbb P\operatorname{div}$ acting on symmetric stresses has an infinite-dimensional kernel consisting of exact stationary states, so no decay estimate can hold for the full stress tensor and the existing sharp-decay theory for dissipative systems does not apply. We identify the active pair $U=(u,\Lambda^{-1}\mathbb P\operatorname{div}\tau)$ as the correct decaying observable and establish, in a critical hybrid Besov framework, a complete characterization of its large-time behavior. For $-d/2<\sigma_1<\sigma\le d/2-1$ we prove that $\|U(t)\|_{\mathcal H^{\sigma}}=O(t^{-(\sigma-\sigma_1)/2})$ holds if and only if the low-frequency part of $U_0$ belongs to $\dot B^{\sigma_1}_{2,\infty}$, and, for $\sigma<d/2-1$, that the two-sided estimate $\|U(t)\|_{\mathcal H^{\sigma}}\simeq t^{-(\sigma-\sigma_1)/2}$ holds if and only if the low-frequency part of $U_0$ belongs to a nondegenerate subclass $\mathfrak B^{\sigma_1}_{2,\infty}$ of $\dot B^{\sigma_1}_{2,\infty}$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi Chen, Mingwen Fei, Lvqiao Liu, Jiahong Wu

item.title: Weighted and Sobolev Estimates for Fractional Schr\"odinger Operators with Reverse H\"{o}lder Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.16274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted and Sobolev estimates for two fractional Schr\"odinger operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $n\geq3$ and $0<s<1$. For the additive operator $L=(-\Delta)^s+V$, with a nonnegative, nontrivial potential $V$ belonging to a suitable reverse H\"older class, $RH_q$, we establish a critical-radius form inequality and decay estimates for the semigroup mass. These yield a heat-kernel bound combining polynomial off-diagonal decay with a fixed positive exponent of decay relative to the fractional critical radius $\rho_s$. A decomposition at this scale gives weighted strong-type estimates for the semigroup maximal operator and weighted Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev estimates for $L^{-\alpha/2}$, $0<\alpha s<n$, together with the corresponding endpoint weak-type estimates. The admissible weights satisfy explicit growth restrictions determined by the kernel decay, and the fractional integration order is $\alpha s$. We also consider the spectral operator $Q=(-\Delta+V)^s$. Assuming $V\in RH_{q_1}$ with $n/(1+s)\leq q_1<n$ and classical critical radius $\rho_1(x)\geq1$, we prove that $\nabla Q^{-1/2}$ maps $H^{1-s,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $1<p\leq p_0$, where $1/p_0=1/q_1-1/n$. By duality, its adjoint maps $L^{p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $H^{s-1,p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $p_0^{'}\leq p^{'}<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Aparajita Dasgupta, Drishti Garg

item.title: Some remarks on nonexistence in the Gamow liquid drop model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we deal with the celebrated Gamow liquid drop model, namely, for $m>0$, $N\geq 2$ and $\alpha\in (0,N)$, we study the problem \[ \min\Big\{P(\Omega)+ V_\alpha(\Omega) : \Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^N,\;|\Omega|=m\Big\}\,, \] and focus mostly on the nonexistence of minimizers for large masses. First we show that any possible minimizer in the asymptotic regime must satisfy an optimal thickness property. Eventually, in the simplified setting of sets made up as a tiling of cubes, we show that nonexistence occurs for large masses for the whole range of parameters $N\geq 2$ and $\alpha\in (0,N)$.
item.dc:creator: Dario Mazzoleni, Aldo Pratelli, Berardo Ruffini

item.title: One-dimensional pressureless flow with a nonlinear velocity law: Bregman variational construction and well-posedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.16341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish global existence, uniqueness and quantitative stability for one-dimensional pressureless flow governed by \[ \partial_t\rho+\partial_x\bigl(\rho f(u)\bigr)=0, \qquad \partial_t(\rho u)+\partial_x\bigl(\rho u f(u)\bigr)=0, \] where $\rho$ is the mass density, possibly measure-valued, $u$ is the physical velocity, and $f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, with $f'>0$, determines the transport velocity $f(u)$. The initial mass has finite positive mass and finite second moment, allowing atoms and unbounded support, and the initial physical velocity is bounded. The difficulty at a cluster collision is that mass and momentum conservation determine a mass-weighted average of physical velocity, whereas transport is governed by the nonlinear law $f$ applied to that average. We construct global entropy solutions by a Bregman variational time discretization whose cost is chosen to reproduce the transport velocity determined by this mass-weighted average, coupled with conditional-expectation updates of physical velocity. For every entropy solution satisfying the Oleinik condition on the transport velocity and initial weak continuity of the kinetic energy measure, we establish a Lagrangian representation and prove uniqueness within this class by comparing flows with possibly different cluster intervals. For two such solutions with the same velocity law and common mass, we obtain a $W_\infty$ estimate for the normalized mass measures in terms of the initial position and physical-velocity discrepancies in mass coordinates, whenever the initial $W_\infty$ distance is finite. The Lagrangian evolution has the semigroup property.
item.dc:creator: Gaowei Cao, Feimin Huang, Guirong Tang

item.title: Spectral stability of resonant Y-solitons for the KP-II equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The KP-II equation was introduced by Kadomtsev and Petviashvili to explain the transverse stability of line solitary waves in shallow water. Using Darboux transformations, we prove the spectral stability of Y-shaped line solitons in an exponentially weighted space that captures the amount of waves receding behind the line solitons. We show that the spectrum of the linearized operator consists of the continuous spectrum of the zero background together with three residual spectral domains whose boundaries contain continuous spectra associated with the constituent line solitons. Exploiting the analytic dependence of the pairings with adjoint eigenfunctions on the spectral parameters, we prove that the orthogonality conditions associated with all adjoint eigenfunctions can be reduced to orthogonality conditions against three families of adjoint continuous eigenfunctions. Moreover, we investigate linear stability of Y-solitons in a subspace satisfying orthogonality conditions against adjoint continuous eigenfunctions associated with outgoing modulations along each line soliton constituting the Y-soliton.
item.dc:creator: Tetsu Mizumachi

item.title: Boundedness and exponential stabilization in a degenerate migration-consumption system with logistic damping
item.description: arXiv:2610.16399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the no-flux problem for a taxis-type migration-consumption system with logistic damping in a bounded planar domain, where the motility function \(\phi\) vanishes at zero and degenerates algebraically of order \(\alpha\ge1\). We prove uniform boundedness in \(L^\infty(\Omega)\times W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)\) for every fixed damping coefficient \(b>0\), without any smallness assumption on the initial data, thus improving the previous \(L^2\)-boundedness results. For \(\alpha>1\), we further prove that the solution converges exponentially to the spatially homogeneous state \((a/b,0)\), with an explicit admissible rate. The proof combines a weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg type inequality adapted to the degeneracy with the dissipative structure of the signal equation. Therefore logistic damping drives the system toward homogeneity, despite the loss of uniform elliptic regularization.
item.dc:creator: Ai Huang, Jing Li, Yifu Wang

item.title: The Inviscid Limit of Viscous Burgers through Shock Formation and Development
item.description:
arXiv:2610.16420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the inviscid limit of the one-dimensional viscous Burgers equation from smooth initial data through nondegenerate shock formation and subsequent shock development. Chaturvedi and Graham \cite{CG} obtained sharp estimates of order $
u^{1/4}$ up to the shock-formation time. We extend their analysis beyond this time, comparing the viscous solution with the inviscid entropy solution evolving from the same initial data. With the shock-formation time normalized to $t=0$, we prove a pointwise error bound on a fixed interval $0\leq t \leq  ar{\varepsilon}$, where $ ar{\varepsilon}>0$ is independent of the viscosity $
u$. The bound consists of a term of order $
u^{1/4}$ and an exponentially localized contribution originating from the viscous shock layer. The proof is based on matching an outer expansion, an inner expansion near the formation point, and a viscous shock-profile expansion. Combined with the results of Chaturvedi and Graham, this yields a quantitative description of the inviscid limit from the initial time through the development of the young shock.
item.dc:creator: Chao Wang, Yueyi Yang, Zhifei Zhang

item.title: Radial pressureless Euler flow: structure and stability of absorption at the origin
item.description: arXiv:2610.16436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study absorption at the origin in radial pressureless Euler flow in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$. For rotation-invariant nonnegative locally finite initial mass and bounded radial initial velocity vanishing at the origin, we prove global existence and uniqueness in a full-space radial entropy class with a one-sided Lipschitz bound and an initial kinetic-energy trace. Absorption is permanent, including retention of any initial origin atom. For finite positive mass with finite second moment, a Lagrangian projection representation characterizes the absorbed mass and its left limits at positive times through extreme minimizers of a free-position primitive. We derive a radial scalar momentum balance with a nonnegative Stieltjes boundary impulse measure. The minimum value of the same primitive yields a weighted Stieltjes identity equating accumulated time-weighted impulse with the integral of initial radii over absorbed labels, valid also for jumps and singular continuous absorption; the boundary impulse measure and the absorption measure are mutually absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$. For such finite-mass data with common total mass, strong $L^2$ convergence of initial quantiles and Lagrangian velocities, together with convergence of initial origin masses, yields convergence of absorbed mass at continuity times of the limiting absorption and local weak convergence of absorption measures on $(0,\infty)$. Finally, even with a fixed smooth initial radial probability density, every probability measure compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$ can be realized as the absorption measure by choosing a bounded radial initial velocity; in particular, purely singular continuous absorption occurs.
item.dc:creator: Gaowei Cao, Feimin Huang, Guirong Tang

item.title: A geometric lower bound for the clamped plate eigenvalue problem in low dimensions and extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the spectrum of the Dirichlet-biLaplacian can be quantitatively bounded from below in terms of the inradius only, for a general open set in dimensions $2$ and $3$. For the same dimensions, we also extend this result to fractional powers $s$ of the Laplacian, with $N/2<s<2$. The resulting estimate comes with a constant having the correct asymptotic behavior as $s$ approaches the two endpoints $N/2$ and $2$. The proofs exploit capacitary techniques in the vein of Maz'ya.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Bianchi, Francesco Bozzola, Lorenzo Brasco

item.title: Asymptotic stability and sharp decay near homogeneous solutions of a nonlinearly damped Schr\"odinger equation on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.16526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the one-dimensional periodic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with a power-type nonlinear damping, both in the focusing and the defocusing regime. For a sufficiently small damping parameter and initial data close in relative $H^1$ norm to a nonzero spatially homogeneous state, we prove global existence and asymptotic convergence, after a constant phase adjustment, to an explicit homogeneous solution. The \(L^2\) and \(H^1\) norms follow the explicit adiabatic decay law, with the same leading coefficient as the homogeneous solution. We obtain explicit convergence rates, including a \(t^{-1/2}\) bound for the relative spatial perturbation. For every nonconstant initial datum in a small neighborhood of the homogeneous solution, the kinetic energy has a strictly positive leading coefficient and decays one power of time faster than the squared \(L^2\) norm.
item.dc:creator: Boris Shakarov

item.title: Minimal time for heat observability on almost-Riemannian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-Riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple Baouendi-Grushin circles. The structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. The formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. Regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. For singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. We also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. Their superpositions give a lower bound for the Schr\"odinger observation time.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Boulard, Amaury Hayat, Emmanuel Tr\'elat
