item.title: Rigidity results for overdetermined problems of p-Laplace equation with spatially dependent data
item.description: arXiv:2610.16686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p>1$ and $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded smooth domain. We study the following overdetermined problem for the p-Laplacian: \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -\Delta_p u=f(x)&x\in\Omega,\\ u=0&x\in\partial\Omega,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial\nu}=g(x)&x\in\partial\Omega, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $\nu$ is the inward unit normal to $\partial\Omega$ and both data may depend on position. A boundary-local version of the moving-plane argument is developed for the possibly degenerate p-Laplace operator. The advantage of this argument is that it avoids the analysis of the degenerate set of the p-Laplacian. Under some reasonable structural conditions, we prove that the solvability of the above mentioned problem forces the domain to be a ball, the source to be radial, and the Neumann datum to be a suitable constant. We also give an explicit formula for the solution. Further consequences include one directional domain symmetry, the conclusion that full rigidity follows from reflection information in any set of directions whose linear reflections generate a dense subgroup of the orthogonal group $O(n)$, and a constant mean curvature characterization.
item.dc:creator: Xi Dai

item.title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.16693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.
item.dc:creator: Hermann Douanla, Hubert Nnang, Joel Fotso Tachago, Jean Louis Woukeng

item.title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with space inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collison part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. Solutions are subject to the physical constraint $0\leq f\leq 1$. Previous existing results have mainly been obtained under suitable smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. A main difficulty stems from the nonlinear and degenerate parabolic structure of the equation. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.
item.dc:creator: Gayrat Toshpulatov

item.title: Sharp Thresholds for Linear Determinacy and Zero Wave Speed in Lotka-Volterra Competition-Diffusion Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.16748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two sharp competition thresholds in the Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion system: the zero-speed threshold for bistable traveling fronts and the linear-determinacy threshold for monostable traveling fronts. Building on our previous results on propagation direction and the classification of traveling waves, we derive explicit Gaussian integral representations of both critical parameters, without involving unknown traveling-wave profiles or speeds. These formulas provide exact characterizations of the optimal competition parameters separating the corresponding propagation regimes. The derivation of these representations was assisted by ChatGPT (OpenAI) Pro, while the underlying theoretical foundations were established in our earlier works.
item.dc:creator: Shizhao Ma, Dongyuan Xiao, Maolin Zhou

item.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $\sigma : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $\Lambda$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in \Lambda} \|\sigma_i -\sigma_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $\sigma_{|\partial \Lambda}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main H\"older regularity statement in a large domain $\Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $\sigma$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the H\"older regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $\sigma \in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial \Lambda}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Garban, Nathan de Montgolfier

item.title: Gauge Transforms and Strichartz Estimates for Benjamin--Ono-Type Dirac Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $T>0$, we consider the Benjamin--Ono-type Dirac equation $$ i\partial_t\psi(x,t) + D(-\Delta)^{\frac{1}{2}}\psi(x,t) = D\,G(\psi(x,t)), \qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,T], $$ where $(-\Delta)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the fractional Riesz operator, $D$ is the Dirac operator associated with the Clifford algebra of signature $(0,n)$, and $G(\cdot)$ a scalar-valued quadratic nonlinearity. Under a pointwise anti-commutation condition on $\psi$ and a uniform dyadic regularity assumption on its spatial Fourier profile, we construct a unit-modulus gauge map $u$ by $ u=\exp\bigl(-iw\bigr),$ where $w$ is a solution of $Dw=\psi$. Assuming, in addition, the stated regularity and commutation conditions on $w$, we show that the Plemelj components $u_{\pm}=P_{\pm}u$ solve a coupled Schr\"odinger system with gauge nonlinearities $P_{\pm}N(\psi,u)$, where $$ N(\psi(x,t),u(x,t)) = -2P_{-}\!\left[ G(\psi(x,t)) \right]u(x,t). $$ We also obtain a priori estimates for the homogeneous Sobolev seminorms $\dot H^\sigma$ of $\psi(\cdot,t)$, with at most exponential growth on $[0,T]$, together with estimates for $P_{\pm}N(\psi(\cdot,t),u(\cdot,t))$. Combining these bounds with the homogeneous and inhomogeneous Strichartz estimates for the Schr\"odinger system, we obtain, for $n\geq 3$ and every sharp Schr\"odinger admissible pair $(q,p)$, an a priori Strichartz-type estimate for $\psi$ in $L_T^q\dot W_x^{\sigma,p}$, expressed in terms of the initial datum $\psi(\cdot,0)$ and the a priori controls of $\psi$ in $L_T^\infty H_x^{\sigma+1}$ and $L_T^\infty L_x^\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Nelson Faustino

item.title: Fundamental solution expansions in stochastic homogenization of parabolic systems with time-dependent coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.16846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies fundamental solutions of uniformly parabolic systems with stationary random coefficients depending on space and time. Under ergodicity and local regularity, we establish quenched Gaussian bounds for the kernel and its spatial derivatives, with stationary random prefactors. A spectral gap assumption gives moments of every finite order for these prefactors and hence annealed Gaussian bounds. We also prove quantitative two-scale expansions for the kernel, its spatial gradient, and its mixed spatial derivative. The error estimates hold in every finite probability moment and retain Gaussian decay. Their dimension-dependent growth is described by a corrector weight, with a single additional logarithmic factor in the derivative estimates. The proofs combine large-scale regularity, extended correctors, weighted estimates, and a parabolic weak-norm estimate. The latter supplies the passage from deterministic pairings to local annealed estimates without interchanging expectation and a supremum over test functions. The mixed-derivative estimate builds on the gradient expansion and does not introduce a further logarithmic loss.
item.dc:creator: Junxin Pan, Li Wang, Qiang Xu

item.title: Limit cycles govern wave energy accumulation in space-time-varying materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.16847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the amplification and concentration of wave energy in smooth, periodic space-time media through the dynamics of the characteristic curves of the associated wave equation. In an impedance-matched setting, we show that stable limit cycles attract neighbouring characteristics, focusing the wave energy density. The exponential attraction rate is estimated analytically from the system's Lyapunov exponent. We further show that the attraction of characteristics and energy accumulation persist under a range of nonperiodic perturbations. Finally, we present a Floquet-Fourier numerical method for computing stable and unstable limit cycles and their attraction rates. Throughout, we exemplify the results using the example of modulation given by a superposition of travelling waves, revealing saddle--node bifurcations where limit cycles may appear depending on the relative wave speeds. Full-wave simulations confirm that the characteristic mechanism continues to describe energy accumulation beyond the impedance-matched case.
item.dc:creator: Bryn Davies, Erik Orvehed Hiltunen

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system
item.description: arXiv:2610.16874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the existence and uniqueness, up to translation, of monotone viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg (NSFK) system, provided the two constant end states satisfy the Rankine-Hugoniot and Lax entropy conditions and the shock strength is small. Treating the small shock strength as a singular perturbation parameter, we construct the profiles via Fenichel's geometric singular perturbation theory. We further provide pointwise estimates for the profiles, which are used in the nonlinear stability analysis of generic Riemann solutions to the NSFK system in a companion work.
item.dc:creator: Sungho Han

item.title: Borderline double phase functionals with powers of the logarithm: regularity in the vectorial case
item.description: arXiv:2610.16900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study vector-valued local minimizers of the borderline double phase functional whose integrand is $|D\mathbf{w}|^p+a(x)|D\mathbf{w}|^p\log^\gamma(e+|D\mathbf{w}|)$, where $p>1$, $\gamma>0$ and the coefficient $a(\cdot)$ is nonnegative and bounded. If the modulus of continuity $\omega(\cdot)$ of $a(\cdot)$ satisfies $\omega(r)\log^\gamma(1/r)\to0$ as $r\to0$, then minimizers are locally H\"older continuous for every exponent less than one. If $a(\cdot)$ is H\"older continuous, then the gradients of minimizers are locally H\"older continuous. In the vector-valued setting these results were previously available only for $\gamma=1$. The proof combines a comparison with frozen functionals, whose regularity theory applies uniformly in the frozen coefficient, with the higher integrability of minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Youlin Choi, Jehan Oh

item.title: Transformed Convexity for Lane--Emden Equations and Torsion on Spherical Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.17012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the geometry of positive Dirichlet solutions on smooth, uniformly geodesically convex domains $\Omega\subsetneq\mathbb S^n$, $n\ge2$. Set $p_n^*=2n/(2n-3)$. For the Lane--Emden equation $-\Delta_g u=u^p$, $1<p\le p_n^*$, we prove that the set of positive solution pairs $(p,u)$ has a connected component containing the near-linear solution curve and projecting onto $(1,p_n^*]$. Every pair on this component satisfies $\nabla_g^2(u^{-(p-1)/3})>0$ in $\Omega$. For the torsion equation $-\Delta_g u=1$, we establish $\nabla_g^2\sqrt{u}<0$ for its unique Dirichlet solution in all dimensions $n\ge2$, without an additional diameter or circumradius assumption. In both settings, the solutions specified above have a unique nondegenerate maximum and strictly geodesically convex positive superlevel sets. For the non-power reaction $f(s)=s^p/(1+\lambda s^\delta)$, with $1<p\le p_n^*$, $\lambda>0$, and $0<\delta\le(p-1)/3$, we also prove the existence of at least one positive solution $u$ for which the transform $\left(\int_u^\infty ds/f(s)\right)^{1/3}$ has positive definite Hessian. The proofs combine a spherical Schur-complement estimate with a priori bounds and continuation.
item.dc:creator: Xiuda Liang, Wenjie Wang

item.title: A cell problem for the boundary density and approximation of boundary correctors in homogenization theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.17026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the boundary corrector $\theta_\epsilon$ in the two-scale expansion for periodic elliptic problems with Dirichlet conditions. By results of G\'{e}rard-Varet--Masmoudi and Prange, on smooth uniformly convex domains $\theta_\epsilon$ converges to the solution $\theta^*$ of a homogenized problem with boundary data given by the boundary layer tail $d(n)$, which is determined by a half-space problem for each normal $n$. In the lifted form of G\'{e}rard-Varet and Masmoudi, $d(n)$ is given explicitly by the cell correctors and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator $N_n$ of this half-space problem. Our main result is that $N_n$ satisfies a nonlinear equation on the period cell alone, so that $d(n)$ and the boundary density that represents it can be computed on the cell. This equation is a Riccati equation in which the derivative in depth is replaced by a commutator with the derivative along $n$. This cell problem can therefore be solved by a Riccati doubling algorithm, and we can compute $d(n)$ at irrational normals without rational approximation. Dropping the commutator term in the cell equation gives an operator square root approximation for $N_n$ that captures the leading term of $d(n)$ for small contrast, for the truncated problem. Finally, we approximate $\theta_\epsilon$ at finite $\epsilon$ by the sum of two solutions of constant coefficient problems, one with oscillatory boundary data and the other $\theta^*$, and test it on the disk.
item.dc:creator: Shari Moskow

item.title: Local Turnpike Stability for Two-Population Second-Order Mean-Field Game Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.17103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes a local turnpike property for a two-population, second-order mean-field game system with a quadratic Hamiltonian, in which the running cost for each population may depend on both population densities. In the case of two populations, imposing a scalar stability condition separately on each species is not sufficient because it neglects cross-interaction effects. The appropriate requirement is instead a matrix-valued coercivity condition on vector perturbations $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$, which involves the symmetric part of the linearized interaction matrix together with weighted Poincar\'e inequalities associated with the two stationary measures. Consequently, in the multi-population framework, diffusion still acts independently on each population, but the interactions are controlled by the full coupling matrix. A naive scalar energy functional fails to capture mixed second-variation terms arising from costs that depend on both densities. We prove that matrix coercivity is precisely equivalent to the strict positivity of this second variation, and we provide a spectral characterization in terms of the principal spectral value of the coupled stationary linearized operator. For linear models with cross-interactions, this yields explicit algebraic conditions that separate stable parameter ranges from unstable ones. In the non-potential framework, the skew-symmetric part of the interaction matrix leaves the coercivity threshold unchanged, but it can induce transient oscillatory dynamics. Moreover, the scalar turnpike theory extends in a natural, though nontrivial, manner to multi-population systems, where stability is governed by the positivity of a coupled matrix-valued second variation that encodes both self-interactions and cross-interactions.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Ghattassi, Fanze Kong, Nader Masmoudi

item.title: Sharp dimension threshold for unique FKPP steady states and BBM recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2610.17121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the existence and uniqueness of positive, bounded stationary solutions of the Fisher-KPP equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish that stationary solutions are unique, and exist if and only if the generalised principal eigenvalue is strictly positive (supercriticality), in dimension at most $6$. This is sharp: we exhibit examples both of non-uniqueness and of existence at criticality in dimension $7$ or higher, including for the classical reaction $f(u)=u-u^2$. This proves a conjecture of Berestycki and Graham in the affirmative for dimension at most $6$, and in the negative for dimension at least $7$. We thereby show that branching Brownian motion cannot survive globally without surviving locally in dimension $6$ or lower, but can do so in dimension $7$ or higher, mirroring the classical transition of Brownian motion from recurrence to transience from dimension $2$ to $3$. We further show that relaxing the strong-KPP condition results in a more general sharp dimension threshold for the uniqueness/non-existence result. These results are valid without any regularity assumptions on the domain boundary. As a corollary, we show that solutions of the evolution reaction-diffusion equation are always convergent in the long run in dimension at most $6$, whilst we exhibit non-convergent solutions in dimension larger than $6$.
item.dc:creator: Luca Rossi, Oliver Tough

item.title: Non-branching properties of Regular Lagrangian Flows and well posedness of the continuity equation in the class of nonnegative solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.17129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we deal with the theory of Regular Lagrangian Flows, as initiated in [29] and axiomatized in [2]. In the first part of the paper we show in Theorem 4.3 (see also Corollary 4.5) that the decomposition of $\mathcal{L}^{1+d}$-almost all the space time in a family of (essentially) disjoint characteristics, the technique at the basis of the well posedness in [1] (for planar, divergence-free and autonomous vector fields), and in [13] (for vector fields having a suitable regularity in space, including BV vector fields) is not only sufficient for well posedness, but also necessary. This shows that in many cases the typical uniqueness statement of the DiPerna-Lions theory, namely that the path $\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ is (essentially) unique given the initial position $x$, can, as in the classical theory, be strengthened by saying that the paths $\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ (essentially) do not branch. As the simple Example 1.1 shows, when we consider vector fields with singular divergence well posedness results may hold only for solutions that do not change sign. In the second part of the paper we revisit [8,9] obtaining a well posedness result for special vector fields of bounded deformation and nonnegative solutions, under a mild regularity assumption (5.3) with respect to the time variable, weaker than the space-time $SBD$ regularity assumption made in [9] for nearly incompressible vector fields. Finally, we revisit carefully the constructions of Section 9 of [13], to see how they provide existence and uniqueness for (1.2) assuming $BV$ regularity in space, in the class of nonnegative bounded solutions.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Ambrosio, Stefano Bianchini, Federico Renzi, Federico Vitillaro

item.title: Local well-posedness for the exponentially modified Benjamin-Ono equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.17182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove local well-posedness for the modified Benjamin-Ono equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$ for $s>3/2$. This equation arises as a modified counterpart of the Benjamin-Ono equation through a Miura-type transformation, in close analogy with the classical relation between mKdV and KdV equations. One of the main obstacles is the apparent derivative loss in the quadratic part of the equation. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a Cole-Hopf transform adapted to the structure of the equation. The map removes the quadratic derivative term and converts the equation into a Schr\"odinger equation with a transport and a commutator terms that can be controlled without derivative loss. Solutions are then constructed by parabolic regularization, while frequency envelopes are used to obtain the continuity of the data-to-solution map. In the degenerate case $\gamma=0$, the transform completely linearizes the equation and yields local well-posedness for every $s>1/2$, down to the scaling-critical threshold.
item.dc:creator: Thyago S. R. Santos

item.title: Multi-peak solutions for a magnetic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with exponential critical growth in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the following magnetic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{i}\nabla-A(x)\right)^{2}u+V(x)u=f(|u|^{2})u\,\ \text{in}\,\ \mathbb{R}^{2}, \] where $\varepsilon>0$ is a parameter, $A\in C(\mathbb{R}^{2}, \mathbb{R}^{2})$ is a magnetic potential, $V\in C(\mathbb{R}^{2}, \mathbb{R})$ is a multi-well potential, and $f\in C^1(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R})$ exhibits exponential critical growth. By variational methods and a penalization technique, we prove the existence and multiplicity of nontrivial solutions for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. If, in addition, $A\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^2,\mathbb{R}^2)$, we show that these solutions have multiple peaks and we establish their concentration behavior and exponential decay.
item.dc:creator: Pietro d'Avenia, Chao Ji, Qingyue Li

item.title: Norm-resolvent asymptotics for the Neumann Laplacian on periodic resonant thin structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.17294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Neumann Laplacian on a three-dimensional periodic network of thin rods with edge thickness of order $h$ and vertex diameter of order $h^{2/3}$. We extend the fixed-graph resonant reduction to obtain a finite-$h$ periodic graph approximation with generalised norm-resolvent error $O(h)$, uniformly in the Floquet quasi-momentum. An exact gauge transformation identifies the phase-corrected graph fibres with the canonical lattice Floquet fibres, giving the same rate for the global operators. Collapsing the contact points while retaining the ambient edge tangents gives an approximation with error $O(h^{2/3})$. The proof uses a Ryzhov boundary triple and a Schur--Feshbach reduction. The estimates yield quantitative approximation of Bloch bands and stability of open gaps on bounded energy intervals. For the simple-cubic lattice, we refine the known resonant dispersion calculation to obtain a complete band-gap decomposition and $O(h)$ control of the persistence of each fixed finite collection of gaps in the thin structure.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Cherednichenko, Chuanjie Wu

item.title: Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.17398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.
item.dc:creator: Solomon Quinn, Charles L. Epstein

item.title: Modeling soliton-potential interactions for the 1-D cubic NLS via an invariant-preserving finite-difference method
item.description: arXiv:2610.17486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1-D focusing cubic NLS with a smooth, spatially-dependent potential which decays rapidly as $x \rightarrow \pm \infty$. As is well known, under sufficient regularity conditions, solutions of the cubic NLS with such a spatially-dependent potential conserve both mass and energy. Additionally, in the absence of a potential, the 1-D focusing cubic NLS admits boosted soliton solutions. Furthermore, in the presence of a potential, the interaction of the potential with boosted soliton solutions to the free case is of active interest in the literature, particularly with respect to the dependence of this soliton-potential interaction on the velocity of the incident soliton. We adapt a finite-difference scheme to the setting of a smooth, rapidly-decaying spatially-dependent potential and show that this adaptation preserves the appropriate mass and energy invariants. Additionally, we use this algorithm to model soliton-potential interactions at a variety of incident soliton velocities.
item.dc:creator: Anthony D. Stone Jr., Christopher C. Hogan

item.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.
item.dc:creator: James M. Hyman

item.title: Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge--Amp\`ere Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.17519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every nonnegative source \(f\in L^1(\Omega)\) in the Monge--Amp\`ere equation \[ \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }\Omega, \] on a bounded uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}\) domain \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(n\geq2\), is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the outward normal derivative and may equal \(+\infty\). For each \(\omega\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\), it suffices to know these slopes for the cylindrical Dirichlet data \[ \frac{t_k^\omega}{2}|P_\omega x|^2,\qquad t_k^\omega\to\infty, \] along any sequence of amplitudes, where \(P_\omega\) projects onto \(\omega^\perp\). The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change-of-variables formula and a large-amplitude limit then recover the Euclidean X-ray transform of \(f\), yielding uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative \(L^\infty\) sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and coincide with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. The argument also extends to \[ \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight \(\vartheta\) is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. Conditional on existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions, the same cylindrical boundary-slope data determine every nonnegative \(L^1\) source.
item.dc:creator: Gunther Uhlmann, Philipp Zimmermann

item.title: Schauder estimate in large scale for compressible planar cavity flows with fast-decaying vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2610.17522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study planar compressible cavity flows fast-decaying vorticity and establish a Schauder estimate in large scale. As an application, we obtain an a priori asymptotic growth rate estimate of the cavity, that $s^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta}\lesssim h(s)\lesssim s^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}$. This is by far the most accurate asymptotic estimate for compressible cavity flows and is probably the first paper that takes vorticity into account in the asymptotic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Chilin Zhang

item.title: Fractional Calder\'on problem with $L^{\infty}$-conductivities
item.description: arXiv:2610.17524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the inverse problem for the fractional conductivity equation with uniformly elliptic conductivities $\gamma\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. For every $n\geq1$ and $0<s<1$, we prove that the local exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on any nonempty open subset of the exterior of a bounded open domain determines $\gamma$ uniquely almost everywhere in $\mathbb R^n$. No continuity, Sobolev regularity, or prescribed behavior at infinity is required. The proof works directly with the conductivity bilinear form and avoids the fractional Liouville reduction. It combines exterior determination at Lebesgue points, equality of weighted solutions, and a unique continuation principle for the fractional Laplacian in the weighted class \[ L_s=\left\{ g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n): \int_{\mathbb R^n} \frac{|g(x)|}{1+|x|^{n+2s}}\,dx<\infty \right\}. \] Specifically, if $g\in L_s$ and both $g$ and $(-\Delta)^s g$ vanish in a nonempty open set, with the latter equality understood distributionally, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. This result requires neither local boundedness nor Sobolev regularity of $g$. Its proof uses the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and boundary unique continuation for the associated degenerate elliptic equation.
item.dc:creator: Gunther Uhlmann, Philipp Zimmermann

item.title: An $\eps$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3-D Navier-Stokes equations and improved upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set
item.description: arXiv:2610.17569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we obtain an $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3D Navier-Stokes equations using a coarse-to-refined estimate argument based on mean-fluctuation decomposition. Making use of this $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion, we improve the upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set to $15/13$.
item.dc:creator: Yi Lu, Rongrong Chi, Wei Ren

item.title: Global existence of large strong solutions to the 3D compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities
item.description: arXiv:2610.17585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional (3D) compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities. By classical $L^p$ estimates to elliptic system, defining suitable energy functions, after the elaborate index analysis, we establish the global existence of strong solutions to the system with all viscosities depending density as long as the initial density is large enough. By product, We also prove the existence of global large strong solutions with only large initial shear viscosity $\mu_1(\rho)$ and angular viscosity $\mu_2(\rho)$, which consists with the research work \cite{ZZ2014} of 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant viscosities and improve the recent result of \cite{HLZ} in some extent where they requiring both initial shear viscosity and bulk viscosity to be large.
item.dc:creator: Tiantian Liu, Xinying Xu

item.title: Existence of positive solutions to anisotropic elliptic equations in the entire Euclidean space
item.description: arXiv:2610.17601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we research an anisotropic elliptic equation in the entire Euclidean space R^{N} . Under the assumption that the nonlinearity of the equation has exponential or critical growth, we prove, by means of the mountain-pass theorem, that the equation admits a nontrivial positive weak solution. Moreover, applying the mountain-pass theorem and Ekeland's variational principle, we show that a perturbation of the equation possesses two distinct positive weak solutions.
item.dc:creator: Rulong Xie, Hailian Wang, Lei Yang

item.title: Global existence of the $s$-Schr\"odinger maps in $n \geq 5$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the $s$-Schr\"odinger map equation \[ \begin{cases} \partial_t u = -u \wedge (-\Delta)^s u \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}\\ u: \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{S}^2\\ u(x,0) = u_0. \end{cases} \] For $s \in (1/2,1)$ and $n \geq 5$ we prove that for small initial data $u_0$ in the critical Besov space one can obtain a global solution.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Dughayshim, Armin Schikorra

item.title: Vanishing viscosity limit of the stationary Navier-Stokes equations in an expanding annulus
item.description: arXiv:2610.17754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish vanishing viscosity limit of the 2D stationary Navier-Stokes equations in an expanding annulus with a fixed width. The flow is subjected to a large perturbation of a rotation of rigid body at one boundary and stays at rest at another boundary. Due to this different boundary condition setting, the boundary layer effects are different near the interior and exterior boundaries, which result in different thickness of boundary layer and different leading order boundary layer equations. We will construct an approximate solution to this 2D Navier-Stokes equations by using higher order asymptotic approximation and show the validity of the boundary layer expansion. The leading order of the Euler solution is the Taylor-Couette flow $\left(Ar+B\frac{1}{r}\right)e_\theta$ for some suitable constant $A$ and $B$, which is determined by using the principle of the Prandtl-Batchelor theory. The perturbation of the tangential velocity becomes large as the annulus expands, which causes heavy difficulties when we show the convergence of the approximate solution. Variously weighted energy estimates up to third-order derivatives of the error solution are constructed to close the energy of the nonlinear system.
item.dc:creator: Xinghong Pan, Chuankai Zhao, Jianfeng Zhao

item.title: Ground states of a logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation with a power perturbation in $\mathbb{R}^N$: existence, uniqueness and nondegeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2610.17766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The objective of this paper is to study the existence and uniqueness of positive ground state solutions of the following Schr\"odinger problem \[ -\Delta u=u\log u^2+\mu\abs{u}^{p-1}u\qquad\text{in }\mathbb {R}^N, \] where $N\ge2$, $1<p<2^*-1$ and $\mu>0.$ We prove that there exists a positive ground state solution for every $\mu>0$ and every such solution is smooth, radially symmetric with respect to some point, strictly decreasing in the radial variable. Moreover, as $\mu\downarrow0,$ the positive ground state solutions centered at the origin will converge, uniformly over the ground-state set, to $U_0(x)=\exp(\frac{(N-\abs{x}^2)}{2})$ in the logarithmic Orlicz--Sobolev space and in $C^{2,\alpha}(\R^N)$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1),$ respectively. Furthermore, for sufficiently small $\mu,$ we also prove that the positive ground state solutions are unique up to translations and the kernel space of the real scalar linearized operator can be spanned by the translation derivatives. The proof combines minimization on the Nehari manifold with uniform compactness and an exterior coefficient estimate that prevents normalized difference and kernel sequences from vanishing locally.
item.dc:creator: Jinqi Yan, Bo You

item.title: Cubic Nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger Systems and Orthonormal Fermionic Ground States in $\mathbb R$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the one-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger system \[ -u_i''-2\Big(\sum_{k=1}^N u_k^2\Big)^{p-1}u_i=\mu_i u_i \quad \mbox{in } \ \mathbb R,\ \ i=1,2,\cdots,N, \tag{S} \] where $u=(u_1,\cdots,u_N)\in H^1(\mathbb{R})^N$, $\mu_1\leq\mu_2\leq\cdots\leq\mu_N<0$, $1<p<3$ and $N\geq 2$ are arbitrary. For the cubic case where $p=2$ and $N\ge 2$, we establish the following structural results of the system $(S)$: (i) all nontrivial solutions can be classified completely; (ii) the linearized operator at any nontrivial solution is non-degenerate; (iii) exact $L^2$-mass formulas of all nontrivial solutions are derived in terms of distinct Lagrange multipliers $\mu_i$. As the applications of the above structural results, we first show that the system $(S)$ with $p=2$ does not have any orthonormal solution for any $N\ge2$. We then investigate a fermionic variational problem $J_N(p)$ with $N\ge2$, whose minimizers correspond to ground states of the system $(S)$ under orthonormal constraints. More precisely, we prove that there exists a sufficiently small $\delta_N>0$ such that $J_N(p)$ is attained for any $p\in(2-\delta_N,2)$, whereas $J_N(p)$ is not attained for any $p\in[2,2+\delta_N)$. These settle some conjectures of [Gontier--Lewin--Nazar, ARMA, 2021] and [Frank--Gontier--Lewin, CMP, 2021].
item.dc:creator: Bin Chen, Yujin Guo, Yong Luo, Juncheng Wei

item.title: Existence of solution for Schr\"odinger-Newton system with vanishing magnetic potential
item.dc:creator: Liying Shan, Wei Shuai, Ping Yang, Jianghua Ye

item.title: Local Hadamard well-posedness of the 2D primitive equations without thermal diffusion under strict stratification
item.description: arXiv:2610.17995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with anisotropic viscosity and no thermal diffusion. For doubly periodic perturbations of a hydrostatic equilibrium with an affine temperature profile, we establish local Hadamard well-posedness in Sobolev spaces under strict stratification. The initial horizontal velocity and temperature have sufficient regularity and vanishing vertical means, but need not be small. The estimates close at the same Sobolev order for these variables despite the horizontal derivative loss in the diagnostic vertical velocity. Stratification-weighted energy estimates and a horizontal compensation argument avoid an additional temperature derivative while retaining the full vertical dependence and the vertically homogeneous velocity component determined by periodic compatibility. A one-sided comparison places higher-order norms of the more regular solution only in terms involving lower-order differences. This structure allows the Bona--Smith method to yield continuous dependence in the original Sobolev topology. We obtain a unique maximal strong solution in the strictly stratified class, together with continuous dependence of the diagnostic vertical velocity and pressure in their natural Sobolev spaces and lower semicontinuity of the maximal lifespan.
item.dc:creator: Fengjie Luo, Quan Wang, Zhengdong Du

item.title: Sobolev Minimizers for Critical Vectorial $p$-Laplacian Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.18002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study minimizers of the optimal Sobolev quotients for the critical embeddings $D^{1,p}(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb R^m)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb R^m)$ and $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$. In the whole space, we classify all minimizers as $\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol c\,U_{\delta,x_0}$, where $\boldsymbol c\neq\boldsymbol0$ and $U_{\delta,x_0}$ is an Aubin--Talenti bubble. On bounded domains and for $\lambda>0$, we equip $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$ with $ \|\boldsymbol u\|_\lambda^p :=\int_\Omega \bigl(|D\boldsymbol u|^p+\lambda|\boldsymbol u|^p\bigr) $. Using scalar attainment results, we establish existence and synchronization of vectorial minimizers. At resonance, we consider the pure Neumann problem $ -\boldsymbol\Delta_p\boldsymbol u =|\boldsymbol u|^{p^*-2}\boldsymbol u\ \text{in }\Omega. $ For the associated quotient, we prove existence and global $C^1(\overline\Omega)$ regularity of minimizers. Finally, we prove synchronization of radial solutions and deduce symmetry breaking on balls.
item.dc:creator: Simone Mauro

item.title: Orthonormal Strichartz estimates over fractal time
item.description: arXiv:2610.18042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Strichartz estimates for orthonormal families of initial data when time is integrated against an $\alpha$-dimensional Frostman measure $\mu$, $0<\alpha\le1$, with coefficients measured in $\ell^\beta$. For the fractional Schr\"odinger, wave and Klein--Gordon equations, we obtain orthogonality gains in the admissible region and necessary conditions on $\beta$. For the fractional Schr\"odinger equation the exponents are sharp up to an endpoint; the optimality of the threshold $\beta=q/2$ requires $\mu$ to be Ahlfors regular. For the Schr\"odinger equation in dimensions $d\ge2$, we prove a Lorentz endpoint estimate and, if $d>2\alpha$, the critical exponent $\beta=q/2$ at every pair $2\le q,r<\infty$ with \[\frac d2(\frac12-\frac1r)\ge\frac\alpha q, \quad r>\frac{dq}{d-\alpha};\] on $r=\infty$ we obtain a restricted weak-type estimate. Since the constants depend on $\mu$ only through its Frostman constant, Lebesgue measure yields global-in-time critical estimates in this range when $d\ge3$. The proofs combine Frostman fractional integration, a spectral near--far argument at the endpoint, and asymmetric Hilbert--Schmidt bounds with orthogonal frequency-block summation. We also obtain further estimates in the low-dimensional cases $d=1$ (fractional Schr\"odinger) and $d=2$ (wave and Klein--Gordon) with $\alpha>1/2$, and formulate the consequences for densities of freely evolving states.
item.dc:creator: Guoxia Feng, Jinbong Lee, Sanghyuk Lee

item.title: Stability Analysis of Bounded Solutions to 2-D Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in L^2_uloc Spaces
item.description:
arXiv:2610.18102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper examines the stability analysis of two-dimensional incompressible fluids in $L^2_{uloc}$ spaces. Extending the classical stability framework for Euler equations in Yudovich-type settings, we establish the convergence of Navier-Stokes solutions toward Euler solutions as viscosity $
u 	o 0$, under the weakened assumptions $u^

Then, using harmonic analysis tools including Littlewood-Paley decomposition and Bony's paraproduct calculus, we prove the $L^\infty$-convergence of the velocity field and $L^2_{uloc}$-convergence of the vorticity as $

item.dc:creator: Haokun Tai, Xiaoxin Zheng

item.title: Multi-dimensional centered rarefaction waves of gas dynamics with vacuum states
item.description: arXiv:2610.18177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Euler equations for a polytropic gas, $p(\rho)=k\rho^{\gamma}$. The $R$--vacuum state--$R$ configuration---two rarefaction waves bounding a vacuum---occurs when the two constant states move apart with sufficiently large relative velocity and is essentially the only vacuum-forming Riemann pattern in the absence of external forces. Local-in-time rarefaction fronts have been constructed only away from vacuum, where the sound speed is bounded away from zero; their construction through the vacuum edge, and hence the structural stability of the $R$--vacuum state--$R$ configuration, has remained open. We establish this stability for $\gamma\in(1,1.3]\cup\{\frac{5}{3},\frac{7}{5}\}$: for sufficiently small perturbations, the Riemann problem admits a continuous entropy solution on a fixed time interval, with the domain partitioned by four characteristic surfaces and the solution in the three central regions belonging to $W^{2,\infty}$ in the self-similar coordinates $(t,x_{1}/t,x_{2})$, even though it may contain logarithmic singularities of the form $c^{\alpha}(\ln c)^{\beta}$ at the vacuum edge. The proof develops a geometric formulation directly on the first-order system, together with a direct analysis of the initial slice at the vacuum edge, where the formal high-order expansion fails.
item.dc:creator: Jin Jia, Tao Luo

item.title: Uniqueness of solutions to the 2D compressible Navier-Stokes equations for bounded densities
item.description: arXiv:2610.18178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the uniqueness of global solutions to the two dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations within the regularity class introduced by Danchin and Mucha [14], for general $C^1$ pressure laws. A crucial assumption is that both solutions have bounded divergence, locally integrable in time, which ensures that their densities remain bounded without excluding vacuum or requiring spatial regularity of the density.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Pescatore, Alessandro Violini

item.title: Interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations $\frac{\sigma_k(D^2u)}{\sigma_\ell(D^2u)}=1$ with $2\leq k\leq n$, $0 \leq \ell < k$, and $k-\ell \in\{1,2\}$. We first adopt the unified quantitative separation-propagation method of Li--Wu [LW26b] to derive a doubling inequality, and then use the compactness argument of Shankar--Yuan [SY25] to obtain the estimates. This approach also applies to a class of general Hessian equations.
item.dc:creator: Zhisu Li, Ke Wu

item.title: Triple Junctions in Multi-Phase Obstacle type Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.18270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the regularity of the free boundary for a multi-phase obstacle-type problem associated to quadrature domains, which arises from the minimization of the energy $$J(U,F):= \int_{B_1} (\frac 1 2 |\nabla U|^2 + F \cdot U)dx$$ among all competitors $U=(u^1,\ldots, u^N)$ with non-negative components $u^i \geq 0$ with disjoint supports, and constant forcing terms $f^i>0.$ We focus on the geometry of the free boundary at points where at least three distinct components meet (triple junctions).
item.dc:creator: Daniela De Silva, Ovidiu Savin, Henrik Shahgholian

item.title: Global well-posedness for a damped two dimensional fluid--beam system
item.description: arXiv:2610.18310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the normalized surface system of an irrotational incompressible fluid of infinite depth beneath an elastic Euler--Bernoulli beam with structural damping. For every fixed damping coefficient $\gamma>0$, we establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial data in $H^2(\R)\times\bigl(\dot H^{1/2}(\R)\cap\dot H^1(\R)\bigr)$. The main novelty is that the admissible data include finite energy initial potentials for which neither $\psi_0$ nor $u_0=\psi_0+G(\eta_0)\psi_0$ has an $L^2$ representative. We also prove the exact energy dissipation identity at the regularity of the constructed solutions. The main analytical difficulties are the possible failure of $L^2$ integrability at low frequencies and the justification of energy differentiation at the solution regularity. To handle the low-frequency difficulty, we fix the low-frequency part of the initial potential and evolving an $L^2$ remainder. Homogeneous Dirichlet--Neumann estimates and a high-frequency Fourier symmetrizer yield local well-posedness with $H^{-1}$ forcing. Continuous Fr\'echet differentiability of the energy in these affine coordinates, together with a chain rule on $H^1\subset L^2\subset H^{-1}$, justifies the dissipation identity. The Energy identity and coercivity provide uniform bounds that yields global continuation tharough the local theory. Iterating the local uniqueness and stability estimates gives global uniqueness within the stated affine solution class and Lipschitz dependence on bounded sets over every finite time interval.
item.dc:creator: Weihua Wang, Lu Yang

item.title: Attainment of the sharp stability constant of Beckner conformal log-Sobolev inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.18327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existence of minimizer for stability of the fractional Sobolev inequality and the stability of Beckner conformal Log-Sobolev inequality (the endpoint case of fractional Sobolev inequality) have been established by K\"onig and Chen-Lu-Tang. The existence of minimizer for stability of the Log-Sobolev inequality is unsolved. In this paper, we solve this problem. For every $n\geq2$, we prove that the sharp $L^2$-stability constant of Beckner conformal log-Sobolev inequality on $\mathbb S^n$ is attained and is strictly less than $\frac{2\log2}{n}$. Moreover, the normalized stability constant of the fractional Sobolev inequality converges to the stability constant of the log-Sobolev inequality as $s\to0^+$. After Hersch normalization, every sequence of $L^{p_{s_k}}$-normalized minimizers for stability of the fractional Sobolev inequality, with $s_k\to0^+$, has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(\mathbb S^n)$ to an $L^2$-normalized minimizer of stability of the log-Sobolev inequality.
item.dc:creator: Lu Chen, Bohan Wang

item.title: Frequency-dependent capacitance matrix formulation for Fabry--P\'erot resonances. Part II: One-dimensional periodic media
item.description: arXiv:2610.18341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Bloch resonances of one-dimensional periodic systems of high-contrast resonators beyond the subwavelength regime. An exact transfer-matrix formulation identifies the limiting wavenumbers with the union of the interior Neumann frequencies and the Dirichlet frequencies of the separating intervals. At each fixed reference wavenumber, we introduce a periodic frequency-dependent capacitance matrix whose positive eigenvalues determine all leading square-root splittings in the contrast parameter. A direct cyclic matching expansion proves the approximation, including multiple eigenvalues and small complex contrasts. A spectral exclusion result outside the limiting set yields a direct bandgap statement. At a common resonance of all intervals, we also derive uniform eigenmode approximations and distinguish the zero-frequency mode from nonzero double Bloch eigenvalues. For positive contrast, exact linear crossings are characterized by the monodromy matrix being proportional to the identity. A complete local classification is obtained for two resonators per cell and, through band folding, for fully symmetric arrays with any number of resonators per cell. We further formulate the weighted Zak phase for isolated bands and its quantization under reflection symmetry. Explicit two-resonator formulas and numerical illustrations complement the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Habib Ammari, Bowen Li, Ping Liu, Yingjie Shao

item.title: Blowup of smooth solutions to 2D quasilinear wave equations with higher-order null conditions and short pulse initial data
item.description: arXiv:2610.18358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the 2D quasilinear wave equation $\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^{2}g^{\alpha\beta}(\partial\phi)\partial_{\alpha\beta}^{2}\phi=0$ with the short pulse initial data $(\phi, \partial_t\phi)|_{t=1}=(\delta^{2-\varepsilon_0}\phi_0(\frac{r-1}{\delta},\omega), \delta^{1-\varepsilon_0}\phi_1(\frac{r-1}{\delta},\omega))$, where $0<\varepsilon_0<1$ is a fixed constant and $\delta>0$ is a small parameter. In our previous work [Ding Bingbing, Xin Zhouping, Yin Huicheng, Sci. China Math., Vol. 69 (2026), No. 3, 667-736], we have established the global existence of a smooth solution $\phi$ under the $k$-th order null condition ($k\ge 2$) when the $(k+1)$-th order null condition fails, provided that $0<\varepsilon_0<\varepsilon_k^*=\frac{k}{k+1}$. As a natural continuation, the present paper demonstrates that for $\varepsilon_0\ge \varepsilon_k^*$, the smooth solution $\phi$ blows up in finite time. Consequently, the threshold $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_k^*$ is shown to be the critical exponent that precisely characterizes the global existence and finite-time blowup for smooth short pulse solutions to the aforementioned 2D quasilinear wave equation, under the assumption that the $k$-th order null condition holds while the $(k+1)$-th order null condition does not. A key novelty of our approach lies in deriving sharp orders of $\delta$ for almost all quantities in both energy and pointwise estimates. This is achieved by utilizing the higher-order null structure in conjunction with a new good unknown recently introduced by us and the transport equation for the difference between this good unknown and its corrector.
item.dc:creator: Bingbing Ding, Zhouping Xin, Huicheng Yin

item.title: Uniform Decay for Ruggeri's Relaxed Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work studies the linearization of Ruggeri's classical symmetric hyperbolic model of viscous, heat-conductive fluids about a homogeneous equilibrium. In three space dimensions, we show that perturbations in $L^1\cap L^2$ decay in $L^2$ at the rate $(1+t)^{-3/4}$, uniformly as a common parameter scaling the three relaxation times tends to zero. The estimate controls the equilibrium variables together with the appropriately weighted stresses and heat flux, and has the same decay rate as the formal Navier--Stokes--Fourier limit.
item.dc:creator: Heinrich Freist\"uhler, Yizhou Zhou

item.title: Dynamic viscoelastic membranes
item.description: arXiv:2610.18466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We rigorously derive a dynamic membrane theory for nonlinear viscoelastic solids with Kelvin-Voigt rheology from the corresponding three-dimensional bulk theory, in the limit of vanishing thickness. The bulk model accounts for inertia, a nonsimple elastic energy depending on the second deformation gradient, and a frame-indifferent dissipation. Orientation preservation is ensured by the energy, while self-interpenetration of the limiting membrane is prevented by a uniform averaged invertibility condition. Our analysis relies on a hyperbolic minimizing movements scheme with two time-scales, which recasts the evolution into a hierarchy of incremental, sequential, and time-delayed problems. For fixed thickness, we prove the existence of solutions to the scheme and their convergence to a weak solution of the continuous-time problem as the time-scales vanish. We then identify the membrane limit at each level of the hierarchy, proving the $\Gamma$-convergence of the incremental functionals and the convergence of solutions to the sequential and time-delayed problems. Since the constant in the Korn inequality is not uniform in the thickness, these limits rely on estimates for the time derivative of the Cauchy-Green tensor rather than for the velocity gradient. Finally, as the outer time-scale vanishes, the membrane time-delayed solutions converge to a measure-valued solution of the membrane continuous-time problem.
item.dc:creator: Martin Kru\v{z}\'ik, Riccardo Voso

item.title: Sign-indefinite transmission conditions and near-zero eigenvalues and resonances
item.description: arXiv:2610.18483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the linear operator for metamaterial modeling $$L_{c,d }=(\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+c)\nabla\!\cdot (\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+d)\nabla\,,$$ where the material parameters $c>0$ and $d$ are constant on each connected component of the bounded domain $\Omega$, $d$ is negative on at least one component of $\Omega$ and transmission boundary conditions hold at the interfaces. It turns out that $L_{c,d }$ has, as in the sign-definite case, an absolutely continuous spectrum equal to $[0,+\infty)$; however, contrary to the latter, it has a non-empty point spectrum; in particular, we find conditions on the parameters so that zero is a threshold eigenvalue. In the case $\Omega$ is connected, we study how such a threshold eigenvalue behaves under $\varepsilon$-small analytic perturbations of the parameters. We show that, depending on the position of the number $\frac12\,\frac{1+d(\ve)}{1-d(\ve)}$ relative to the nearest eigenvalue of the Neumann-Poincar\'e operator of the interface, the zero eigenvalue splits into two branches (analytic in $\varepsilon^{1/2}$), consisting either of two branches of resonances, or of one branch of negative eigenvalues and one of resonances.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Mantile, Andrea Posilicano

item.title: Viscosity Solutions for Hamilton-Jacobi equations on Separable Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work provides a framework to treat optimal control problems on separable Banach spaces in the viscosity sense. First, it extends the notion of $B$-viscosity solutions to the Banach setting and relates the extension to the notions of viscosity solutions used in metric space settings. As the main results, the paper proves a strict comparison principle and characterizes the value function of an optimal control problem as the unique viscosity solution to an infinite-dimensional HJB equation.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Fuchs

item.title: Near-boundary rigidity and strict maximum modulus for Neumann eigenfunctions on convex planar domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.18546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the maximum modulus of every nonzero second Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded convex planar domain $\Omega$ is attained only on the boundary, without boundary smoothness or eigenvalue simplicity. The key is a rigidity theorem for any positive Neumann eigenvalue $\mu$: an interior maximum-modulus point $p$ with $\sqrt{\mu}\,\operatorname{dist}(p,\partial\Omega)<\pi/\sqrt{3}$ forces the domain to be a rectangle and the eigenfunction to be a cosine of one coordinate. In particular, $\mu\ge4\mu_2(\Omega)$, and the factor $4$ is sharp. This result reveals how a local distance condition at a single interior maximum-modulus point can enforce global geometric rigidity, thereby linking extremum localization to the classification of domains and eigenfunctions.
item.dc:creator: Haiyun Deng, Xuyong Jiang, Xiaoping Yang

item.title: Generic boundary behavior of Dirichlet eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Uhlenbeck's classical results on the generic properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions. In particular, we find a residual set of $C^k$ domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $k > n$, such that the nodal set of any Dirichlet eigenfunction intersects the boundary orthogonally along a $C^{k-1}$ embedded submanifold, whenever the intersection is non-empty. This is achieved by analyzing the boundary asymptotics of Dirichlet eigenfunctions via homogeneous harmonic polynomials and comparing their respective nodal sets. Along the way, we give a complete proof that generic Euclidean domains have simple Dirichlet eigenfunctions with zero as a regular value in the interior and zero as a regular value of the boundary normal derivative. In the special case of planar domains, a different argument provides one-parameter families of perturbed domains with the desired properties.
item.dc:creator: Alec Payne, Zihui Zhao

item.title: Generalized minimizers for the capillarity energy outside convex obstacles
item.description: arXiv:2610.18673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In general, the capillarity energy outside an unbounded obstacle may fail to admit volume-constrained minimizers, as infimizing sequences may escape to infinity. We study this minimization problem outside a closed convex obstacle $C$. Via a $\Gamma$-convergence result for the capillarity energies outside sequences of closed convex obstacles converging in the Hausdorff sense, we prove that the infimum of the functional is attained by a generalized minimizer, namely, a finite union of regions, each of which minimizes the capillarity energy outside a limit of translations of $C$ in its volume class, with the total volume satisfying the prescribed constraint. Each generalized minimizer can be suitably approximated by an infimizing sequence, thus providing a description of its asymptotic behaviour. As an application, we study the isoperimetric profile associated with the capillarity energy and investigate how the asymptotic geometry of the obstacle affects both this profile and generalized minimizers and their connectedness.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Nani, Simone Vincini

item.title: Optimal transport to non-convex polyhedral domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.18756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal transport with a non-convex polyhedral target in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The closure of the singular set is locally a smooth hypersurface outside a relatively closed set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-2$. For partial transport between domains separated by a hyperplane, the source free boundary has the same regularity.
item.dc:creator: Shibing Chen, Qi-Rui Li, Yuanyuan Li, Jiakun Liu, Xiaotian Wu

item.title: Sharp Global Well-Posedness for the Logarithmically Regularized $2$D Euler Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Euler equations with a logarithmically regularized velocity given by $u=\nabla^{\perp}(-\Delta)^{-1}\ln^{-\gamma}(|\nabla|+e)\omega$ and initial vorticity in $\dot{H}^1 \cap \dot{H}^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $\gamma>1/2$, then global well-posedness holds.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Radke

item.title: Global existence of smooth solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations for initial data with infinite energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.18797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the global existence of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations for any divergence-free distributional initial data. The solutions are smooth in both time and space at positive times. When the initial data belong to the Sobolev spaces $W^{-1,p}$ for $1<p<\infty$, our constructed solutions are weak in the classical sense. We also characterize the distributional initial data admitting weak solutions and obtain the sharp ranges in Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Cheskidov, Hedong Hou

item.title: The rhombic dodecahedral conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.13975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every three-dimensional parallelohedron $P$ satisfies \[ \mathcal H^2(\partial P)\ge 12\sqrt2\,r(P)^2, \] where $r(P)$ is the inradius of $P$, with equality if and only if $P$ is similar to the regular rhombic dodecahedron.
item.dc:creator: Annalisa Cesaroni, Matteo Novaga

item.title: Intrinsic Contraction Theory and Stabilization of Probability Measures on the Wasserstein Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.14164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deterministic flows can contract Wasserstein distances between probability laws without being contractive in point-state space. We develop a differential contraction theory for pushforward flows on forward-invariant subsets of the 2-Wasserstein space that quotients out the gauge freedom of the continuity equation. Weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition and the Wasserstein contingent cone define the weighted horizontal tangent cone (whtc). Requiring the contraction quadratic form to be nonpositive only on the whtc yields the Intrinsic Wasserstein Contraction Condition (IWCC), which generalizes the classical contraction LMI and recovers it on Dirac measures. An almost-everywhere Euler approximation based on the superposition principle and Banach-valued Lebesgue differentiation theorem proves that IWCC is sufficient for intrinsic Wasserstein contraction. Law contraction without point-state contraction is illustrated by a rotationally symmetric shear example. Finally, a new comparison lemma yields an incremental Wasserstein ISS theorem; for Brockett's integrator, we prove exponential stabilization of a class of axisymmetric laws to the uniform law on a circle via a smooth feedback.
item.dc:creator: Min Kim, Joshua D. Ibrahim, Soon-Jo Chung

item.title: Volume growth and parabolicity for non-symmetric operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.14375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interplay between a weighted volume measure and its naturally associated weighted Laplace operator is fundamental to the geometric analysis of weighted structures governed by gradient vector fields. Beyond the gradient setting, however, the theory has remained considerably less developed, largely because this natural correspondence is lost. In this paper, we identify invariant measures as the appropriate framework for extending the theory to general drifted Laplace operators. This approach yields a systematic treatment of parabolicity in the non-gradient setting, reveals its connection with volume growth, and leads to new volume finiteness results for non-gradient geometric structures.
item.dc:creator: Leandro F. Pessoa, Stefano Pigola, Alberto G. Setti

item.title: A new convergence proof for an iterative scheme for elliptic Cauchy problems based on alternating orthogonal projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.14600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider an elliptic Cauchy problem for the Poisson equation in which both Dirichlet and Neumann boundary data are prescribed only on a portion of the boundary, while no boundary conditions are available on the remaining part of the boundary. Such problems are severely ill-posed. In this work, we study the convergence of an iterative method based on the alternating imposition of Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. We formulate the scheme within a Hilbert space framework, where a yet another alternation becomes apparent: each iteration can now be interpreted as an orthogonal projection onto an appropriate closed subspace. This perspective provides a transparent geometric interpretation of the algorithm and yields a concise convergence proof based on von Neumann's classical result on alternating (orthogonal) projections. In addition to elucidating the convergence of the method, this alternating projections perspective also offers a general rate of convergence in terms of the Friedrichs angle (between two closed subspaces). We point out by means of an example that such convergence rate estimate degenerates for the elliptic Cauchy problem under consideration.
item.dc:creator: Abhijit Guchhait, Adrian Muntean, Martin Lind

item.title: Global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.14870v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation with a positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side on a compact K\"ahler manifold.
item.dc:creator: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang, Kai Zheng

item.title: Continuous meets discrete: geometry dependence of the performance of iterative solutions for nonsymmetric PDEs in terms of Laplace eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2610.14946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is a classical fact in spectral geometry that the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian depend continuously on the geometry of the underlying domain, under suitable geometric restrictions. We show that this theoretical property is reflected in a concrete numerical situation: the convergence rate of iterative solvers for convection-diffusion problems remains stable under deformations of the domain. The connection is a superlinear estimate for preconditioned GMRES/GCR in which the relative residual errors are bounded by an explicit expression of the eigenvalues of the Laplacian, or of a symmetric positive elliptic operator in divergence form. We prove that this bound depends continuously on the domain, uniformly in the iteration index, under either regularity hypotheses on the boundary or a topological constraint in dimension two. We also establish corresponding statements on the discrete level. Two examples delimit the theory: domains bounded by a fractal curve, where continuity still holds, and perforated domains, where it fails. The theoretical results, including both examples with rough domains, are confirmed by numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: F. Francesconi, J. Kar\'atson, B. Lados, J. Rowlett

item.title: Dimensional transition and spectral instability in lattice Hardy inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.14950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discretization can change a sharp stability threshold even when the continuum threshold is recovered at infinity. We study this phenomenon for the Hardy inequality on the integer lattice in dimensions at least three: its best coefficient agrees with the continuum value through dimension eight and is smaller from dimension nine onwards. We characterize this transition by the total critical defect, the summable error obtained by testing the lattice operator against the critical continuum power. A theta-function representation proves that the defect is negative and strictly decreasing from dimension nine; explicit positive Hardy remainders establish its positivity in dimensions three through eight. An exact energy identity relates this defect to the energy saved by optimizing the profile outside the neighbours of the origin. This exterior remains stable in dimensions eight and nine, locating the first loss of positivity in its coupling to those neighbours. We give self-contained proofs of both dimensional ranges. We then describe how local attraction creates a negative eigenvalue in a general class of lattice operators with critical inverse-square tails. Its magnitude is exponentially small near the threshold, with both the rate and the multiplicative prefactor determined by zero-energy solutions. The result allows connected finite modifications of the lattice and nonradial corrections to the tail. The same analysis controls the spread of the emerging state and gives a two-dimensional return scale for the associated Markov chain in every ambient dimension.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Lizama

item.title: Weak universality of global dynamics for the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model
item.description: arXiv:2610.15135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the study of weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model initiated by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). In this work, we establish weak universality in a regime where the associated Gibbs measure is mutually singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We first investigate the weak convergence of the Gibbs measures associated with macroscopic models to the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure constructed by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). We then obtain a structured representation for these Gibbs measures via the stochastic quantization method. Finally, we prove dynamical weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model by using an extended second order expansion and exploiting the invariance of the Gibbs measures.
item.dc:creator: Ruoyuan Liu

item.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is neutrally stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Daniels, Simon Eskin, Tel Fahrendholz, Arnd Scheel

item.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.15736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.
item.dc:creator: Allen Weitsman

item.title: An optimization problem for $\delta'$ leaky stars
item.description: arXiv:2610.15771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider singular Schr\"odinger operators with an attractive $\delta'$ interaction of strength $\beta$ supported by a star graph and prove that the ground-state eigenvalue is uniquely maximized by stars of the maximum symmetry. Two different proofs are presented, one for an even number of edges using a comparison to the $\delta$ interaction star, the other general based on Birman-Schwinger technique.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner

item.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for singular $L^k$ interaction kernels with rates
item.description: arXiv:2610.15852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Based on a semigroup approach, we prove quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for two systems of interacting particles with singular interaction kernels $K$ of type $L^k$, $k>d$, and a contractive Lipschitz confinement force field. First, we consider a system with moderate interaction, which means that the particles interact through the mollified kernel $K\ast V^N$, for some approximation of identity $V^N = N^{d\alpha} V(N^\alpha \cdot),\, \alpha>0$. Assuming that $\|K\|_{L^k}$ is sufficiently small, we obtain that for any $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform-in-time rate is of order $N^{-\min\left(\alpha,\frac12-\frac{d\alpha}{2}-\varepsilon\right)}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. Second, for the classical, non-mollified particle system we establish uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with rate $N^{-\min\left(\alpha,\frac12-\frac{d\alpha}{2}-\varepsilon\right)} + \|K-K\ast V^N\|_{L^{k}}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. The method relies on the regularity properties of the solution of the associated nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation combined with estimates of the Duhamel formulation of the mollified empirical measure, together with partial Girsanov transforms for the non-mollified system of particles.
item.dc:creator: Nicoleta Cazacu, Alexandre Richard, Milica Tomasevic

item.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of K\"ahler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform \`a priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.
item.dc:creator: Johannes G. Scheffler

item.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.15984v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.
item.dc:creator: Hoan Nguyen

item.title: (Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schr\"odinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+\delta}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $\delta>0$. In the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model.
