The constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. This provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast Chernoff approximation formulated by Remizov in Problem 30 of arXiv:2410.00416.
item.dc:creator: Comlan Edmond Koudjinan

item.title: Large deviation principles for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations on unbounded channel-like domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.16381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates the large deviation principle for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations driven by multiplicative noise and defined on an unbounded channel-like domain. We first prove the existence and uniqueness of probabilistically strong solutions for the stochastic equation under small noise perturbations by means of the local monotonicity method. Subsequently, we show the well-posedness of solutions to the corresponding control equation and the convergence in distribution of the solutions for the stochastic equation as the noise intensity tends to zero. Finally, we establish the Freidlin-Wentzell type large deviation principle for the solutions of the stochastic equation by using the weak convergence method. To overcome the lack of compactness of Sobolev embedding on unbounded domains, we employ a scalar stream function together with a truncation technique to derive uniform tail estimates for the solutions of the control equation.
item.dc:creator: Gang He, Ji Shu, Huixia Wen, Longyu Wu

item.title: Reverse H\"older Class and Two-Parameter Good-$\lambda$ Inequality over Hausdorff Content
item.description: arXiv:2610.16405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical harmonic analysis is built upon Lebesgue (or more general) measure. Such a framework is remarkably successful for sets of full ambient dimension, but becomes intrinsically insensitive to lower-dimensional geometry: curves, surfaces, and more generally fractal subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\) with zero \(n\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In contrast, Hausdorff content provides a dimension-sensitive notion of size for lower-dimensional sets or fractal sets, but harmonic analysis in this setting is still largely limited to maximal operators. In this paper, we establish a weighted two-parameter good-\(\lambda\) inequality under Hausdorff content setting, providing a route toward other general operators from maximal operators over Hausdorff content. To do this, we firstly identify an appropriate reverse H\"older class $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,\delta}$ associated with Hausdorff content, and then prove the self-improving property of $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,\delta}$ by establishing the fundamental equivalence between reverse H\"older weights and capacitary Muckenhoupt weights. As direct applications, we obtain weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality and some boundedness on general operators over Hausdorff content. The methodology developed in this paper, even when reduced to the Lebesgue measure case, also provide novel insights, which shows that the good-\(\lambda\) principle is not intrinsically tied to an underlying measure, but can extended to a non-additive framework.
item.dc:creator: Long Huang, Yangzhi Zhang, Ciqiang Zhuo

item.title: On the Weyl tube formula for nonlocal perimeters
item.description: arXiv:2610.16461v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the nonlocal perimeter of tubular neighbourhoods. For a closed $C^{1,1}$ submanifold of Euclidean space, we show that a suitable rescaling of the nonlocal perimeter of its tube converges to an explicit constant times the Hausdorff measure of the submanifold. The constant is the fractional perimeter of the unit ball in the codimension of the submanifold. For finite point sets, we obtain an exact tube formula in terms of a generalised hypergeometric function. In contrast with the classical Weyl formula, this expansion has infinitely many terms, contains both noninteger and integer powers of the tubular radius, and has coefficients that depend on the relative positions of the points rather than only on their intrinsic geometry. We also establish a point-set expansion for general analytic kernels.
item.dc:creator: Serena Dipierro, Jack Thompson, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: Long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus (CKE) equation extends the coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) equation by adding quintic and derivative nonlinearities. We study the Cauchy problem for the focusing CKE equation with Schwartz initial data under the assumption of no discrete spectrum and no spectral singularities on the real axis. Based on the gauge equivalence between the focusing CKE and CNLS equations, we analyze the associated $3\times3$ matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem by the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. By establishing joint error estimates for the CNLS solution and the gauge phase, we obtain a uniform long-time asymptotic formula for the dispersive radiation of the CKE equation with an $O(t^{-1}\log t)$ remainder in bounded velocity cones.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_\theta$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Lefeuvre

item.title: Analytical and numerical periodic homogenization of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations in a $W^{2,p}$ Cordes framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.17142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study periodic homogenization of fully-nonlinear second-order Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations subject to a homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition and the numerical approximation of the effective Hamiltonian, where the diffusion matrix is assumed to satisfy the Cordes condition. In the first part, assuming the Cordes parameter is sufficiently large, we show existence and uniqueness of $W^{2,p}$ solutions to the true cell problem, prove homogenization under minimal regularity assumptions, and establish a quantitative homogenization result. In the second part, we propose and rigorously analyze $W^{2,p}$-conforming and mixed finite element methods for the approximation of the corrector, which are then used in the approximation of the effective Hamiltonian. The key tool used throughout this work is Campanato's concept of near operators.
item.dc:creator: Timo Sprekeler, Hung V. Tran

item.title: Resonance counting and spectral gaps for hyperbolic surfaces via Fourier decay
item.description: arXiv:2610.17276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an improved fractal Weyl upper bound for resonances of infinite-area convex cocompact hyperbolic surfaces, expressed in terms of the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set and the Fourier decay exponent of the Patterson--Sullivan measure. This bound also yields a sharper upper bound for the essential spectral gap for these surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Louis Soares

item.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
item.description: arXiv:2610.17307v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) \zeta_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $\zeta$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{\alpha-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $\alpha \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Pr\"omel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $\zeta = dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.
item.dc:creator: Tim Van Hoose

item.title: Kinetic SDEs and kinetic Fokker-Planck equations with critical Morrey-type drifts, and local blow-ups
item.description: arXiv:2610.17319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a Sobolev theory for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation subject to a singular Morrey-form $L^\infty+M^q_K$ force field which can produce local blow-ups due to strong attraction to a submanifold. Our approach is based on the fractional representation for the Duhamel series of the equation and on establishing kinetic Adams-type estimates. Accordingly, we construct weak solutions of Brownian-driven kinetic SDEs in a critical Morrey set-up, obtain kinetic Krylov-type estimates and a strongly continuous Feller propagator, and establish uniqueness criteria for a large class of weak solutions.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Jabir, Damir Kinzebulatov, Chengjun Yue

item.title: Large Deviations of Invariant Measures of Fractional Reaction-Diffusion Equations Driven by Multiplicative Noise on R^n
item.description: arXiv:2610.17491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish large deviations of invariant measures for fractional stochastic reaction-diffusion equations with polynomial reaction term driven by unbounded multiplicative noise on R^n. Under a dissipativity condition, we first prove the Freidlin-Wentzell large deviation principle of solution trajectories uniformly over all initial data in L^2(R^n). The key ingredient is a positive-time L^\infty-estimate for differences of controlled solutions which is independent of all initial data and hence yields uniform convergence of controlled stochastic solutions over the entire tphase space. Then using the uniform trajectory estimates, contraction and a second-moment estimate, we further prove the large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with a good quasipotential without introducing weighted spaces or establishing exponential tightness. The non-compactness of Sobolev embeddings in R^n is circumvented by uniform spatial tail-ends estimates. This is the first result on large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with multiplicative noise on unbounded domains.
item.dc:creator: Bixiang Wang, Lu Yang

item.title: Sharp Damping Location for Stability of a Locally Damped Wave Equation and its Galerkin Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.17539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the stability of the variable coefficient wave equation $u_{tt}-u_{xx}-(1+x^{2})u_{yy}+\chi_{\mathbb G}u_{t}=0$ on the rectangle $(-1,1)\times(0,\pi)$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the viscous damping acts on a vertical strip $\mathbb G=(\eta-\delta,\eta+\delta)\times(0,\pi)$. We establish a precise relationship between the location of the damping region and the rate of energy decay. We prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable whenever the closure of the damping strip meets the line $x=0$, i.e., $|\eta|\leq\delta$, despite the existence of rays that never enter the damped region. When the damping region is strictly bounded away from $x=0$, the semigroup decays at the sharp rate $(\log(2+t))^{-1}$. The proofs combine separation of variables, one-dimensional resolvent estimates, a reflection identity for the harmonic oscillator, and Gaussian quasimodes. We then consider the spectral Galerkin approximation based on the Dirichlet eigenfunctions of the constant coefficient Laplacian and show that, although the sequence of semigroups resulting from the approximation converges to the continuous one, it fails to be uniformly exponentially stable.
item.dc:creator: Kangsheng Liu, Lihui Lu, Qiong Zhang

item.title: Classical and quantum scattering of massive Klein--Gordon fields in asymptotically flat spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17819v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use microlocal tools to define distinguished incoming and outgoing vacuum states of the quantum theory of massive Klein--Gordon fields in non-trapping asymptotically flat spacetimes, including radiative perturbations of Minkowski space. The asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the Hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum S-matrix is well-defined. These results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the Klein--Gordon equation. Our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Molodyk

item.title: Dynamical BEC formation and vanishing entropy for trapped bosons in non-relativistic QED via nonlinear resonance cascades
item.description: arXiv:2610.17923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The dynamical formation of a complete Bose-Einstein condensate and the asymptotic purification of trapped bosons coupled to a quantized radiation field are rigorously established. By tracking the macroscopic one-particle density matrix $\kappa_T$ through a nonlinear resonance cascade, it is demonstrated that radiative relaxation irreversibly depletes all excited trap modes, even when the initial macroscopic state $\kappa_0$ is genuinely mixed. Here $\kappa_T$ is an average, with respect to a de Finetti measure $\mu_0$, over mean-field particle-field orbits, so that the mixedness of $\kappa_0$ reflects a statistical ensemble of orbits. Under the assumptions of a non-vanishing initial ground state component and strictly positive downward Fermi-Golden-Rule rates, strong trace-norm convergence to a pure condensate is proven, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty} \| \kappa_T-|\chi_0\rangle\langle\chi_0| \|_{\mathfrak{S}_1(\mathfrak{h})} = 0 \, . $$ Furthermore, the von Neumann entropy of the macroscopic one-particle density matrix is shown to vanish asymptotically, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty}S[\kappa_T]=0 \, , $$ without any claim of monotonicity in $T$. Thus, any initially mixed, positive-entropy state ($0<S[\kappa_0]<\infty$) is purified to the ground state $|\chi_0\rangle\langle\chi_0|$. For the proof, we derive the Hartree hierarchy of the coupled system of bosons and photons from the finite-$N$ BBGKY hierarchy of the microscopic quantum many-body system, establishing trace-norm convergence in the mean-field limit as $N\to\infty$. The limits are taken successively; first $N\to\infty$, then the weak-coupling limit, and finally $T\to\infty$. Although the global particle-field evolution remains unitary, the macroscopic one-particle state converges to a pure state as energy and correlations are continuously radiated into the dispersive field.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Chen, Ali Mezher

item.title: Eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.18013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the eigenvalues of the negative Dirichlet Laplacian $-\Delta$ in domain $D_{\epsilon,N}$ obtained by removing $N$ Euclidean balls of radius $\epsilon$ from a bounded open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ ($d\ge2$). It is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $\rho$ and for $N\to\infty$ and $\epsilon\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate Newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $\kappa>0$, the eigenvalues of $-\Delta$ in $D_{\epsilon,N}$ homogenize to those of the Schr\"odinger operator $-\Delta+\kappa\rho$ in $D$. Here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate Central Limit Theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. Unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by Figari, Orlandi and Teta and, independently, Ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Marek Biskup, Ryoki Fukushima

item.title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.18219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. These provide infinite family of Einstein metrics on closed $4$-manifolds with $\lambda>0$, which are in addition not Hermitian. We further establish the uniqueness of the $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics on $S^4$, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and CP^2#\bar{CP}^2.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Broder, Ramiro A. Lafuente

item.title: One-way pressure-independent valves with hysteresis and chattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.18242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a model for the one-dimensional isothermal gas flow through a valve in a pipe. The valve aims at keeping the outgoing flow in an assigned interval; moreover, its opening and closing depend on a further parameter. The model is realized by a system of two conservation laws with suitable conditions coupling the ingoing and the outgoing flow. We study the corresponding Riemann problem, where non-classical shocks show up. Although simple, the model allows to study two key oscillatory behaviors of the flow, which are due, respectively, to the chattering of the valve, especially seen in the numerical simulations, and to the stabilizing hysteresis induced by the valve operation. We characterize the states leading to chattering and show how they depend on the parameters of the model. Through several numerical simulations, we study the interplay between the two above phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Bagagiolo, Andrea Corli, Stefan Moreti, Massimiliano D. Rosini

item.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.18599v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.
item.dc:creator: Antonio De Rosa, Aria Halavati

item.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

item.title: Branching explosion of Brownian Fleming-Viot systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.18802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve the long-standing non-extinction problem for Brownian Fleming-Viot systems in bounded domains. For every fixed N >= 3, we construct a bounded connected domain in R3 in which branching explosion occurs with positive probability before every prescribed positive time, from every interior initial configuration. On this event all particles converge to one boundary point. Together with two-particle non-extinction, this gives the sharp population threshold for bounded-domain Brownian explosion. The mechanism is directed transport generated by uniform copying in a periodic absorbing environment. We compute a positive cubic current for the same two-harmonic killing profile at every N >= 3, with an explicit population coefficient and a controlled fourth-order remainder. To realize this transport by spherical absorption, we develop a marked genealogical transfer theorem that retains the Euclidean displacement inherited at each copy. Common ancestry makes the integer winding reconstructible from phase records and yields convergence of the stationary signed current. A boundary restart law with P'olya weights supplies the continuity needed to turn that current into stable escape. Diffusion coefficients adapted to a common Kelvin clock preserve the joint Brownian law and uniform donor marks while compressing escape into finite lifetime. Disjoint spherical holes in a ball accumulate only at the explosion point. The boundary is smooth elsewhere, with finite area and perimeter. Boundary area within distance r of the singularity is of order r. For three particles, the transfer theorem covers every smooth positive periodic killing rate.
item.dc:creator: Yaohui Lin, Tiankui Lu

item.title: Exterior free-boundary minimal surfaces of every topological type with at least two ends
item.description: arXiv:2610.18832v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface in the complement of the open unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. We prove that for all integers $\ell\geq2$, $b\geq1$ and $\gamma\geq0$ there is a connected, orientable, properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with $\ell$ ends, $b$ boundary components and genus $\gamma$. Its total curvature is finite, and its ends are parallel catenoidal ends of multiplicity one. By the theorem of Mazet and Mendes, a surface of this kind with one end is a rotational annulus. Hence the topological types of such embedded surfaces are exactly the annulus with one end and all types with at least two ends. There are two gluing constructions. For $\ell\geq3$ we stack $\ell$ sheets over a stable catenoidal annulus that meets the sphere along a circle of radius $4/5$, and we join adjacent sheets by half-catenoidal bridges sitting on the sphere. The sheets are small normal graphs over this annulus whose displacements contain different multiples of the Jacobi field of the family of such annuli, so their boundary circles and the logarithmic growth of their ends differ slightly. For $\ell=2$ we double a catenoidal annulus near the critical angle $\pi/4$, where it acquires a bounded rotationally invariant Jacobi field; the distance to the critical annulus is coupled to the size of the bridges. In gluing constructions inside the unit ball that double or stack a compact surface, the bridges themselves must balance the sheets, which forces many bridges. Here the logarithmic growth of the ends absorbs this balancing. A fixed number of bridges therefore suffices, and every topological type is reached, including the small ones.
item.dc:creator: Igor Kozyrev

item.title: Suppression of blow-up in the 3D Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system via non-parallel shear flows
item.description: arXiv:2401.15982v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the three-dimensional Patlak-Keller-Segel system coupled with the Navier-Stokes equations near the non-parallel shear flow $( Ay, 0, Ay )$ in $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$. We show that if the shear flow is sufficiently strong (A is large enough), then the solutions to Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system are global in time without any smallness restriction on the initial cell mass as long as the initial velocity satisfies $A^{\frac{2}{3}}\|u_{\rm in}\|_{H^2}\leq C_0$, which seems to be the first result of studying the suppression effect of shear flows for the 3D Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system. Moreover, it implies that the solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations are global in time if the initial velocity satisfies $A^{\frac{2}{3}}\|v_{\rm in}-(Ay,0,Ay)\|_{H^2}\leq C_0,$ which also shows the transition threshold for the shear flow $(Ay,0,Ay)$ in $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$.
item.dc:creator: Shikun Cui, Lili Wang, Wendong Wang

item.title: Quantization analysis of Moser-Trudinger equations in the Poincar\'e disk and applications
item.dc:creator: Lu Chen, Qiaoqiao Hua, Guozhen Lu, Shuangjie Peng, Chunhua Wang

item.title: Existence and Smoothing for a Nondivergence-Form Degenerate Diffusion from Plasma-Wave Theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.13922v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove existence, positive-time smoothing, and physical admissibility of weak solutions to the degenerate parabolic Cauchy-Dirichlet problem $\partial_t u = \rho_\lambda(x) u \partial_x^2 u + \rho_\lambda(x) g(x) u$ on the half-line, where $\rho_\lambda$ vanishes at the boundary and grows at infinity. This scalar problem arises by formally reducing the system of equations given by the quasilinear theory of plasma waves in the one-dimensional case. This theory models a background distribution of electrons $f$ coupled to a spectral energy density $W$ through wave-particle resonance. For the scalar problem we construct weak solutions from weighted $L^p$ initial data and bounded reaction, admitting the unbounded, discontinuous data that the physical model demands, and lying beyond the reach of the continuous-data theories developed for nearby problems. We identify a parabolic smoothing effect for the constructed solution, namely one-sided bounds on $\partial_t u$: from merely integrable data, the solution becomes locally H\"older in space and time and locally Lipschitz in space at positive times. This spatial regularity is shown to be sharp by explicit examples. Finally, we address the quasilinear system itself, whose well-posedness remains open: we prove that the scalar solution induces a particle-wave pair $(f^{\ast}, W^{\ast})$ which is a weak solution of the system. Under nonnegativity and finite-moment hypotheses on the initial data, both components remain nonnegative and the initial mass is conserved. Moreover, the pair inherits positive-time regularity, with $W^{\ast}$ decaying quantitatively at large wavenumber and $f^{\ast}$ smoothing to a locally bounded function even when initially a measure.
item.dc:creator: William Porteous, Irene M. Gamba, Kun Huang

item.title: Quantitative and exact concavity principles for parabolic and elliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2504.09494v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Goal of this paper is to study classes of Cauchy-Dirichlet problems which include parabolic equations of the type $$u_t -\Delta u= a(x,t)f(u)\quad\hbox{in $\Omega\times(0,T)$}$$ with $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ bounded, convex domain and $T\in(0,+\infty]$. Under suitable assumptions on $a$ and $f$, we show logarithmic or power concavity (in space, or in space-time) of the solution $u$; under some relaxed assumptions on $a$, we show moreover that $u$ enjoys concavity properties up to a controlled error. The results include relevant examples like the torsion $f(u)=1$, the Lane-Emden equation $f(u)=u^q$, $q\in(0,1)$, the eigenfunction $f(u)=u$, the logarithmic equation $f(u)=u\log(u^2)$, and the saturable nonlinearity $f(u)=\frac{u^2}{1+u}$. The logistic equation $f(x,u)=a(x)u-u^2$ can be treated as well. Some exact results give a different approach, as well as generalizations, to [Ishige-Salani2013, Ishige-Salani2016]. Moreover, some quantitative results are valid also in the elliptic framework $-\Delta u=a(x)f(u)$ and refine [Bucur-Squassina2019, Gallo-Squassina2024].
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: Section A Mathematics. Published online 2026:1-54
item.dc:creator: Marco Gallo, Riccardo Moraschi, Marco Squassina

item.title: Local asymptotics for singular solutions to critical Hartree equations
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Henrique Andrade, Tao Feng, Paolo Piccione, Minbo Yang

item.title: Transverse dependence and asymptotic dimensional reduction of ground states for the logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation on a waveguide manifold
item.description: arXiv:2505.23403v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel approach to studying the $y$-dependence of ground states for the logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}$. Unlike in \cite{STNT2014} (Analysis \& PDE, 2014) and \cite{HH1} (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 2024), the power-law scaling argument does not transfer directly to the logarithmic setting. Instead, amplitude scaling gives an exact identity showing that transverse dependence is independent of the prescribed mass. We also discuss uniqueness for the Cauchy problem and conditional orbital stability.
item.dc:creator: Jun Wang, Hichem Hajaiej, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: On the singular set of the free boundary for a Monge-Amp\`ere obstacle problem
item.description: arXiv:2506.08387v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is a continuation of our earlier work [14] on the Monge-Amp\`ere obstacle problem \[ \det D^2 v = v^q \chi_{\{v>0\}}, \quad v \geq 0 \text{ convex} \] with $q \in [0,n)$, where we studied the regularity of the strictly convex part of the free boundary. In this work, we examine the non-strictly convex part of the free boundary and establish optimal dimension bounds for its flat portion. Additionally, we investigate the strong maximum principle and a stability property for this Monge-Amp\`ere obstacle problem.
item.dc:creator: Tianling Jin, Xushan Tu, Jingang Xiong

item.title: On Singular Integrals and Quantitative Rectifiability in Parabolic Space and the Heisenberg Group
item.description: arXiv:2510.26934v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: David and Semmes proved that if all CZOs (of suitable dimension) are bounded with respect to an Ahlfors regular measure, then the measure is uniformly rectifiable. We extend this theorem to the parabolic space and to all Heisenberg groups.
item.dc:creator: John Hoffman, Benjamin Jaye

item.title: Locally uniform ellipticity of the fractional Hessian operators
item.description: arXiv:2511.10034v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In [1], Caffarelli-Charro introduced a fractional Monge-Amp\`{e}re operator. Later, Wu [21] generalized it to a fractional analogue of $k$-Hessian operators and proved the strict ellipticity for $k=2$. In this paper, we introduce a fractional analogue of general Hessian operators and prove the stability. We also show that the fractional analogue $k$-Hessian operators defined in [21] are uniformly elliptic for all $2\leq k\leq n$.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Gan, Heming Jiao

item.title: Multiple positive bound states for NLS equations on noncompact metric graphs with potential
item.description: arXiv:2602.18894v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish the existence of geometrically distinct bound states for the subcritical Nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger (NLS) equation on a noncompact metric graph, provided that the mass is sufficiently large. By bound states we mean critical points of the NLS energy functional constrained to the manifold of fixed $L^2$-norm. We demonstrate that the NLS equation admits at least as many positive bound states as the number of bounded edges of the graph. Our approach is purely variational and relies on a doubly constrained minimization procedure. It is worth noting that, compared with the case where the potential vanishes, the scaling structure of solitons is destroyed here. Moreover, the classical energy asymptotic behavior $\mathcal{E}(\phi_{\mu},\mathbb{R})=-\theta \mu^{2\beta+1}$ is no longer preserved.
item.dc:creator: Q. Liu

item.title: Local boundedness for weak solutions to fractional porous medium equation
item.description: arXiv:2602.23001v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish local boundedness for solutions to fractional porous medium-type equations in the fast diffusion regime, under optimal tail assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Filomena De Filippis

item.title: On the passage from nonlinear to linearized viscoelastodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2603.02988v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The equations of linearized viscoelastodynamics in Kelvin-Voigt rheology are rigorously derived from a nonlinear model that satisfies the time-dependent frame indifference in the sense of Antman. Besides showing the convergence of corresponding solutions of both systems, we also prove the convergence of time-discrete solutions on various scales and of continuous solutions of nonlinear problems to linearized ones.
item.dc:creator: Barbora Bene\v{s}ov\'a, Malte Kampschulte, Martin Kru\v{z}\'ik

item.title: Point interactions and singular solutions to semilinear elliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2603.08487v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the connection between semilinear elliptic PDEs with isolated singularities and stationary nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with point interactions. In dimensions $d=2,3$, we establish a rigorous correspondence between their solutions, revealing two regimes depending on whether a boundary condition at the singularity can be imposed. This connection enables us to exploit operator-theoretic and variational methods that have not previously been applied to the study of isolated singularities. In the source regime, we prove the existence of infinitely many radial singular solutions, by applying the symmetric mountain pass theorem of Ambrosetti and Rabinowitz to the action functional associated with the point interaction. When $d=2$, a suitable uniqueness result allows us to characterize singular ground states (positive solutions) as action minimizers and to prove the existence of infinitely many nodal singular solutions.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Boni, Diego Noja, Raffaele Scandone

item.title: On a thermodynamically consistent diffuse interface model for incompressible two-phase flows with unmatched densities: Energy equality and Lyapunov stability
item.description: arXiv:2603.26020v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the initial-boundary value problem of a thermodynamically consistent diffuse interface model for incompressible two-phase flows with unmatched densities in a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$. Our first aim is to study the energy equality for global weak solutions by establishing mixed $L_t^qL_x^r$-regularity conditions on the velocity field, its gradient, and its time derivative, under which the global weak solution satisfies the energy equality for all times. The proof is based on the propagation of regularity for weak solutions to the convective Cahn-Hilliard equation with a physically relevant Flory-Huggins-type potential, combined with global mollification and boundary cut-off techniques. Next, we prove the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions in the general setting with non-constant gradient energy coefficient and non-degenerate mobility, provided that the initial velocity is sufficiently small and the initial phase-field variable is a sufficiently small perturbation of a local minimizer of the free energy. This yields Lyapunov stability for each steady state consisting of a zero velocity together with a local energy minimizer. The proof relies on the energy equality for (local) strong solutions and the {\L}ojasiewicz-Simon approach.
item.dc:creator: Harald Garcke, Maoyin Lv, Hao Wu

item.title: Symmetry and critical points of second Neumann eigenfunctions on isosceles trapezoids and kites
item.description: arXiv:2604.19003v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the symmetry and multiplicity of the second Neumann eigenvalue on isosceles trapezoids and kites as the height varies. Precisely, away from a unique transition height, the second Neumann eigenvalue is simple, and its eigenfunction is either symmetric or antisymmetric. At a transition height, it has multiplicity two, with one symmetric and one antisymmetric basis eigenfunction. We prove that every nonzero real second Neumann eigenfunction has no interior critical points, including arbitrary linear combinations at a transition height, thereby verifying the \textit{hot spots conjecture} for both classes of domains. In the simple-eigenvalue case, we also classify the nonvertex boundary critical points for trapezoids and kites. Reflection reduces the spectral classification to a comparison of a Neumann branch and a mixed Dirichlet--Neumann branch. Energy estimates establish strict transversality at every crossing and hence uniqueness wherever a transition occurs. To treat the two-dimensional eigenspace, we use Jacobian estimates and directional and radial comparison arguments to exclude cancellation of the two basis gradients.
item.dc:creator: Haiyun Deng, Changfeng Gui, Xuyong Jiang, Xiaoping Yang, Ruofei Yao, Jun Zou

item.title: Liouville Theorems for Stationary Navier-Stokes Equations via the Radial Velocity Component
item.description: arXiv:2605.05647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Liouville-type results for the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We prove that any $\dot{H}^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ solution is trivial under an integrability condition imposed only on the radial component of the velocity, namely $u_\rho(x) \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^3)$ with $3/2 < p \leq 3$. We also establish a uniqueness result in a variable-exponent setting, where an $L^6$-type condition is required only on a bounded region, while the exponent approaches the critical value $3$ at infinity. Our analysis reveals that the rigidity of the stationary Navier--Stokes system can be driven by localized and radial integrability properties, rather than uniform global conditions.
item.dc:creator: Gaston Vergara-Hermosilla

item.title: Regularity for degenerate or singular fully nonlinear elliptic equations with Hamiltonian terms and applications
item.description: arXiv:2606.11607v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate regularity properties for viscosity solutions to a general class of degenerate or singular fully nonlinear elliptic equations with Hamiltonian terms, \[ \left\{ \begin{alignedat}{2} \Phi(|Du|,x)F(D^{2}u,x)+H(|Du|,x) & =f(x) \quad && \text{in } \quad \Omega,\\ u(x) & = g(x) \quad && \text{on } \quad \partial\Omega. \end{alignedat} \right. \] Here, $F$ is uniformly elliptic, while $\Phi$ and $H$ satisfy suitable structural and growth conditions allowing for both degenerate and singular regimes. Our first result establishes sharp global $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity for this general class of equations, thereby providing a unified regularity framework for both degenerate and singular regimes. We next develop an oscillation-based approach for fully nonlinear equations with unbalanced variable degeneracy and Hamiltonian terms. Under a H\"older-type decay assumption on $ f $, we derive sharp boundary $C^{1,\beta'}$ estimates with an explicit exponent, and establish a quantitative non-degeneracy estimate in the singular region. Finally, as applications of the general theory, under a suitable viscosity curvature condition on the level sets of the solution, we establish global $ C^{1,\frac{1}{3}} $ regularity for the infinity-Poisson and global $ C^{1,\frac{1}{p-1}} $ regularity for the $ p $-Poisson with $ p>2 $. These results may provide a new perspective on these two long-standing open problems.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwen Wang, Feida Jiang

item.title: Inverse Problems for the Monge-Amp\`ere Equation: Linearization and Nonlinear Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2606.13939v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study inverse boundary value problems for the fully nonlinear Monge-Amp\`ere equation $ \det D^2u=a(x,u,\nabla u) $ in a bounded domain. Motivated by Calder\'on-type problems, we introduce nonlinear Cauchy data and investigate the recovery of $a$ from boundary measurements. Around a strictly convex background solution, under a sign condition ensuring invertibility of the linearized Dirichlet problem, we establish local well-posedness and differentiable dependence on boundary data. The first variation yields a linear elliptic operator with principal coefficient given by the cofactor of the background Hessian and lower-order coefficients determined by derivatives of $a$. An Alessandrini-type identity reduces equality of nonlinear measurements to an anisotropic Calder\'on problem. Conditional on uniqueness for this linear problem, we recover the first derivatives of $a$ along the background jet. Higher-order linearization yields integral identities whose inversion depends on a product-density property. We also establish unconditional uniqueness results in special settings. For $\det D^2u=f(x)$, local nonlinear Cauchy data determine $f$ in dimension two, and in higher dimensions under real-analytic anisotropic hypotheses. We compare this result with a planar small-data method and an all-dimensional large-data approach based on the Euclidean X-ray transform. For semilinear nonlinearities around $\Phi(x)=|x|^2/2$, Schr\"odinger inverse results recover the accessible $z$-jet. For equilibrium optimal-transport nonlinearities, linearization yields an isotropic conductivity equation and uniquely determines the transport density.
item.dc:creator: Gunther Uhlmann, Philipp Zimmermann

item.title: Geometric approaches for improved regularity in fully nonlinear parabolic models
item.description: arXiv:2606.24617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we derive improved estimates for a class of fully nonlinear parabolic equations with continuous drift and admissible source terms of the form $$ \partial_{t}u - F(D^2u,x,t) + \langle B(x,t), Du\rangle = f(x, t, u^{+}, u^{-}) \quad \text{in}\quad Q_1. $$ Our analysis reveals two distinct regimes. In the first, $f=f(x,t)$ exhibits $\theta$-H\"{o}lder decay ($\theta\in(0,1)$), yielding improved gradient regularity at vanishing points via perturbative methods and geometric iteration, as well as nondegeneracy with explicit growth rates under a suitable structural condition. In the second, $f(\cdot,u^+,u^-)=(u^+)^\gamma-(u^-)^\gamma$ with $\gamma\in(0,1)$ (corresponding to an evolutionary semilinear two-phase model), we obtain enhanced regularity at branching points by combining a robust blow-up analysis with local derivative estimates for linear equations. Our results remain relevant even in linear settings with merely continuous data, linking to classical free boundary problems arising in mathematical physics and related areas.
item.dc:creator: Junior da Silva Bessa, Jo\~ao Vitor da Silva, Mayra Soares

item.title: The local Cauchy problem for hyperbolic systems of equations with fractional dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2606.26887v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for a class of hyperbolic quasilinear evolution systems with fractional dissipation and commutators of the fractional Laplacian $(-\Delta)^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha\in(0,1)$. The analysis is motivated by the compressible isentropic Navier-Stokes equations with fractional diffusion and the compressible Euler alignment system with singular communication weights. We show that the contribution of the commutators to the energy is absorbed by the dissipation. Our approach does not rely on the cancellation condition previously used to recover the coercivity of the highest-order non-local terms. We further show that the commutator term induces a loss of regularity in the stability estimates, preventing the standard contraction argument from being applied. Therefore, we instead establish the relative compactness of the solution operator and apply Schauder's fixed point theorem. The resulting theory provides local existence for arbitrary orders $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and identifies the obstacles to local uniqueness in the presence of fractional commutators.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Angeles

item.title: The nonlocal attraction-repulsion transport equation with power kernels
item.description: arXiv:2607.04424v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a nonlocal continuity equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ in which a probability density is driven by the competition between attraction toward a prescribed background measure $\omega$ and self-repulsion among particles, governed respectively by the power-law kernels $\psi_a(x) = |x|^{1+a}$ and $\psi_r(x) = |x|^{1+r}$ with exponents $a, r \in [0,1)$. We establish global Lagrangian well-posedness via a squared-radius regularization, obtaining {finite-time $L^\infty$ and moment bounds}, $W^{n,\infty}$ regularity, and uniqueness in the Lagrangian class. When the initial data is compactly supported and attraction dominates ($a > r$, or $a = r$ with $\omega(\mathbb{R}^d) > 1$), we prove that the support remains uniformly bounded at all time; a counterexample shows this fails for $a = r > 1$. For the attractive-dominant nonquadratic range $0 \leq r \leq a < 1$, we characterize zero-flux stationary states via a free-boundary problem involving a fractional Laplacian operator, reducing the stationarity condition to a fractional exterior Dirichlet problem. This characterization allows us to exhibit explicit examples of stationary measures in dimensions $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. Numerical particle simulations {are consistent} with the theoretical stationary profiles. Finally, for $0 \le r \le a < 1$, we prove that every global solution whose energy is bounded from below and whose moments are bounded uniformly in time converges, along a sequence of times, to a zero-flux stationary state. Full narrow convergence follows whenever the omega-limit set contains a single stationary state.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Fornasier, Hui Huang, Lukang Sun

item.title: $L^{2}-L^{\infty}$ decay estimates and inviscid limits for Global smooth solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Riesz system
item.description: arXiv:2607.05562v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ for the repulsive compressible Navier-Stokes-Riesz system with Riesz exponent $0<s<1$ and viscosity $0<\varepsilon\leq1$, where the Riesz interaction $\nabla(-\Delta)^{-s}(\rho-\bar{\rho})$ is a generalization of the Coulomb interaction for electrons. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium, with the solenoidal component of the initial velocity of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions. We derive time-decay estimates in $L^{2}$ norms and $L^{\infty}$ norms that capture both uniform-in-$\varepsilon$ dispersive behavior and viscosity-dependent dissipation. We further establish a global-in-time inviscid limit to the irrotational global solution of the compressible Euler-Riesz system whose initial data consist of the same density and the curl-free component of the velocity, with an explicit convergence rate in $W^{k,p}$ norms. The proof combines viscosity-adapted dispersive estimates, normal-form analysis and nonlinear energy estimates with control of both negative and positive Sobolev norms.
item.dc:creator: Agnieszka \'Swierczewska-Gwiazda, Yuan Xu, Junhao Zhang

item.title: Logarithmic Depletion of Vortex Stretching and Singularity Evasion in the 3D Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.08866v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a geometric-analytic mechanism for the suppression of finite-time singularities in the 3D incompressible (unforced) Navier-Stokes equations for critical point singularities exhibiting $L^{3/2, \infty}$ spatial concentration of vorticity. We demonstrate that if the vorticity direction resides locally in a logarithmically weighted space of bounded mean oscillations, $\mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ -- a space failing the Dini condition and thus permitting wild oscillatory defects -- the nonlinear vortex stretching is fundamentally depleted. By isolating a unidirectional geometric cancellation, we recast the stretching eigenvalue as a singular integral commutator. Utilizing a localized Coifman-Rochberg-Weiss estimate coupled with dyadic BMO tail bounds, we prove the stretching potential vanishes as a logarithmic envelope on shrinking super-level sets. This depletion forces the vorticity magnitude into a sub-critical Lorentz-Zygmund space via interpolated De Giorgi energy method. The logarithmic gain is subsequently transferred to the velocity field, forcing the geometric scale of local 1D sparseness below the uniform radius of spatial analyticity, ultimately averting the finite time blow-up via the harmonic measure maximum principle.
item.dc:creator: Zoran Grujic

item.title: A Dacorogna-Moser construction of transport maps on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with application to geodesics on the space of couplings
item.description: arXiv:2607.23241v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A seminal work by Dacorogna and Moser introduced a way of constructing regular transport maps from a probability distribution on a bounded domain to another one. In this work, we extend this construction to the whole $\mathbb{R}^d$ for strictly asymptotically log-concave measures, a wide class of distributions that encompasses Lipschitz-perturbations of log-concave measures. We then leverage this construction to study geodesics in the space of probability measures on a product set with imposed marginal laws (couplings), for which we derive optimality conditions, answering an open question in a recent work by Conforti, Lacker and Pal. Taking inspiration from Brenier's variational model for incompressible fluids and its regularization, we further introduce an entropic regularization of the geodesic problem, which can be seen as the Schr\"odinger bridge problem on the space of couplings, for which we also derive optimality conditions. We eventually study convergence of minimizers as the regularization vanishes, and we prove convergence of the related Lagrange multipliers. Our approach involves proving uniform-in-time global regularity estimates on elliptic and parabolic equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$, by exploiting the structure of asymptotically log-concave measures using the probabilistic notion of reflection coupling.
item.dc:creator: Louis-Pierre Chaintron, Matteo Picco

item.title: A nonlinear Li-Yau inequality and its consequences
item.description:
arXiv:2608.28881v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp nonlinear analogue of the Li-Yau inequality for positive solutions of the normalized parabolic $p$-Laplacian equation \[ u_t = \Delta u + (p-2)|
abla u|^{-2}
abla^2u(
abla u,
abla u),\ \ \ 1<p<\infty, \] on a closed Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the equation being interpreted in the viscosity sense on the critical set of the solution. We also derive a sharp global Harnack inequality from the gradient estimate. The constant is best possible. Equality holds identically for an explicit self-similar solution in $\Rn$, and sharpness on closed manifolds follows by taking the limit along the flat tori $\mathbb R^n/(L\mathbb Z)^n$ as $L 	o \infty$. The proof rests on an exact Bochner-type identity for a family of uniformly parabolic approximating flows. We choose the first-order term separately from the second-order regularization so that the maximum principle yields the sharp constant, uniformly in the regularization parameter and without any assumption on the critical set of the solution. Using this Bochner identity with a modified Li-Yau functional, we extend the estimate to closed manifolds with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Agnid Banerjee, Nicola Garofalo, Hamidreza Mahmoudian

item.title: Parabolic Poincar\'e inequalities and maximal function estimates for systems of partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.03830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study parabolic Poincar\'e inequalities for solutions to nonlinear systems of partial differential equations. Our main results show that these inequalities are self-improving. As applications, we establish reverse H\"older inequalities for the mean oscillation over parabolic cylinders and for the gradient. We also consider the corresponding Poincar\'e inequalities and self-improvement results on time intervals at fixed spatial points. These results are based on a pointwise maximal function estimate. As an application, we obtain regularity results in the time direction for solutions to nonlinear systems.
item.dc:creator: Wontae Kim, Juha Kinnunen

item.title: On Decay of the Local Mean Oscillations of the Vorticity Direction in Critical Navier-Stokes Flows
item.description: arXiv:2609.05720v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We isolate and analyze the geometric PDE governing the evolution of the vorticity direction in the 3D incompressible (unforced) Navier-Stokes equations (NSE), restricted to the case of a critical spatial point singularity where the vorticity magnitude concentrates as $O(|x|^{-2})$, inhabiting the critical Lorentz space $L^{3/2, \infty}$. The PDE consists of the Harmonic Map Heat Flow (HMHF) into the sphere supplemented with the fluid transport, cross-diffusion and tangential strain. The question is whether the NSE mechanics can propagate logarithmic decay of the local mean oscillations of the direction -- the condition $\xi \in \mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ -- which (in this setting) was shown in the companion paper to prevent finite time blow-up. A key observation is that the $O(|x|^{-2})$ concentration, factored out of the viscous cross-diffusion, generates an outward radial drift $4\nu\, x/|x|^2$ at the core. Under a suitable condition we prove a barrier lemma for the total drift-diffusion operator and show that the HMHF nonlinearity is harmless for the quantity $\frac12|\xi - e|^2$ which is a subsolution on any hemisphere. This yields a transfer theorem: the $\mathrm{bmo}_{1/|\log r|}$ regularity of the direction at the core, uniformly up to the singular time, is controlled by a logarithmic modulus in time of the direction at the inner scale, together with the physical strain. Crucially, the strain enters the direction equation only through its tangential component which vanishes precisely when the direction is an eigenvector of the strain tensor. Since this includes the eigenvector carrying the maximal stretching, the result is in contrast to the classical geometric regularity theory which is built on depleting the full vortex-stretching term and thus confined to configurations of weak stretching.
item.dc:creator: Zoran Grujic

item.title: Determination of Wave Speed from point sources
item.description: arXiv:2609.06225v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the wave equation with variable wave speed in Euclidean space, with point sources modeled by Dirac delta initial displacement data. There are three special subsets of the whole space: (1) the source set where the delta initial conditions are supported, (2) the unknown set where the wave speed is not known a priori, and (3) the receiver set where the waves are measured. The inverse problem is to reconstruct the wave speed uniquely in the unknown set from an unlabeled collection of waves generated by point sources and measured in the receiver set. We use propagation of singularities and sharp finite speed of propagation to reduce this data to geometric travel-time data, whose form depends on how the three sets lie in relation to each other. We give three scenarios where this procedure leads to unique determination of the wave speed.
item.dc:creator: Joonas Ilmavirta, Teemu Saksala, Ashwin Tarikere, Gunther Uhlmann

item.title: Fully discrete stochastic maximal regularity and $H^\infty$-calculus for second-order elliptic operators
item.description:
arXiv:2609.07436v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper establishes the fully discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-regularity and the accompanying sharp maximal estimate for numerical approximations of parabolic stochastic partial differential equations. We consider the spatial finite element discretization $A_h$ of a general second-order elliptic operator $A=-
abla \cdot a
abla +b\cdot 
abla +c$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a smooth, bounded, convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, coupled with a broad class of temporal schemes, including rational approximations and the exponential Euler method. To obtain these optimal discrete regularity results, we establish a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus for the discrete spatial operator $A_h$, uniformly in the mesh size $h$. As a direct byproduct, we also establish the discrete-in-space stochastic maximal regularity for the corresponding spatial semi-discretizations. As an application, we establish the pathwise uniform convergence of a fully discrete approximation of the three-dimensional stochastic Allen--Cahn equation with variable diffusion coefficients and multiplicative noise.
item.dc:creator: Foivos Evangelopoulos-Ntemiris

item.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.17712v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce several notions of resonance for systems exhibiting weak or partial dissipation: $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, with $A$ the generator of a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. We refer to resonance as the phenomenon where a time-periodic $f$ may yield an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, unbounded growth may depend on topological choices, and several ``resonances" may occur. Classically, existence of $T$-periodic $u$ under $T$-periodic $f$ is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. Consequently, its failure permits unbounded solution growth and we elucidate that connection through properties of $S(t)$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and provide an associated resonance taxonomy. The growth rate of ~$||(A-\lambda I)^{-1}||_H$ on ~$i\R$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$, and, for rapid growth in $\lambda$, that gap can be infinite. In this case, we demonstrate implications for periodic solvability, and a mechanism for constructing smooth resonant forces. The theory developed here is motivated by (and demonstrated for) a hyperbolic-parabolic system, where the latter component provides the only system dissipation. Such dynamics are a simplification of fluid-structure phenomena, which demonstrate strong stability but do not provide unconditional periodic well-posedness. Though point-spectral resonance is ruled out, we note that $\mathcal R(I-S(T))\neq H$. Our main result here shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, a classical heat-wave system possesses periods $T$ which yield infinite derivative loss and, via supporting results, yield resonance with smooth forcing.
item.dc:creator: Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster

item.title: Sharp regularity results for eikonal equations in Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.20145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Viscosity solutions of eikonal equations need not enjoy regularity beyond Lipschitz continuity. In contrast, differentiable solutions exhibit stronger structural properties. In the Euclidean setting, building on observations of Caffarelli and Crandall (Comm. Partial Differential Equations $\textbf{35}$ (2010), 391--414), one finds that differentiable solutions of the eikonal equation $\| Df \| \equiv 1 \,\, \text{in } \mathcal{U} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ are of class $C^{1, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal U)$. Moreover, if $\mathcal{U} = \mathbb{R}^d$, then $f$ must be affine. This manuscript revisits these phenomena in the setting of (finite-- and infinite--dimensional) Banach spaces. Our results show how the geometry of the underlying Banach space determines the regularity and affineness of Gateaux--differentiable solutions of eikonal equations. As a geometric application in finite dimensions, we characterize differentiable functions whose gradient ranges are constrained to boundaries of convex bodies.
item.dc:creator: Tr\'i Minh L\^e, Sebasti\'an Tapia-Garc\'ia

item.title: Korn and Poincar\'e-Korn inequalities for thin domains in $GSBD^p$
item.description: arXiv:2609.21261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Korn's first inequalities with and without boundary conditions in $GSBD^p$ ($1<p<\infty$) in $C^{1,1}$-regular thin domains with Lipschitz thickness boundaries with a constant $C h^{-p},$ that is optimal if the domain mid-surface contains a flat region, e.g., if the domain contains a piece of plate. For the one with boundary condition, we impose zero Dirichlet boundary conditions on the thin lateral faces of the shell, where we prove that the same estimate holds with no subtracted rigid motion like in the classical case for Sobolev vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Davit Harutyunyan

item.title: Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Compressible Nematic Liquid Crystal Flows with Large Initial Data and Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2609.23764v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate two-dimensional compressible nematic liquid crystal flows with a planar director. We assume that the shear viscosity is a positive constant and that the bulk viscosity is given by $\lambda(\rho)=\rho^\beta$ with $\beta>4/3$. In the periodic domain or in a bounded simply connected smooth domain with Navier-slip and Neumann boundary conditions, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions without any restrictions on the size of the initial data. In particular, no geometric angle condition is imposed on the initial orientation field. Moreover, we derive a time-uniform upper bound for the density and establish exponential decay estimates for the strong solutions.
item.dc:creator: Qinghao Lei, Lu Wang

item.title: Global Well-Posedness of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Compressible Nematic Liquid Crystal Flows with Large Initial Data and Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2609.23770v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the two-dimensional barotropic compressible nematic liquid crystal flows with a planar director in the whole space or in the half-space. Under the assumptions that the shear viscosity is a positive constant and that the bulk viscosity is given by $\lambda(\rho)=\rho^\beta$ with $\beta>4/3$, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. It should be mentioned that our results are obtained without any restrictions on the size of the initial data and allow for the presence of vacuum. In particular, the initial orientation field is not required to satisfy any geometric angle condition.
item.dc:creator: Qinghao Lei, Lu Wang

item.title: A sharp two-disk bound for the second positive Neumann eigenvalue under a curvature upper bound
item.description: arXiv:2609.26609v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the sharp two-disk comparison conjectured by Langford and Laugesen for the second positive Neumann eigenvalue under an upper Gaussian-curvature bound, and strengthen it to a shifted reciprocal inequality. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}$ be bounded, simply connected and Lipschitz, with $g=\omega|dz|^2$, where $\omega$ is continuous and positive on $\overline{\Omega}$ and $\Delta\log\omega+2K\omega\ge0$ in distributions. Write $A=|\Omega|_g$ and enumerate the spectrum by $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$. If $KA<4\pi$ when $K>0$, then $\frac{1}{\lambda_2}+\frac{1}{\lambda_3}>\frac{2}{\lambda_1(D_K(A/2))}$ and $\lambda_2<\lambda_1(D_K(A/2))$, where $D_K(A/2)$ is the constant-curvature disk of area $A/2$. The same conclusions hold for disk-type Lipschitz domains in smooth surfaces. In the subcritical regime, both bounds are sharp, as witnessed by an extremizing sequence of smooth connected domains of exact area and curvature whose Neumann eigenvalues converge, at every fixed index, to those of two disjoint equal model disks. At $KA=4\pi$ we obtain the sharp non-strict bounds $\lambda_2\le2K$ and $\lambda_2^{-1}+\lambda_3^{-1}\ge K^{-1}$. The proof combines two-pole Green coordinates, positive-kernel comparison, and simultaneous centering. We also establish a global quadratic deficit for the model area split.
item.dc:creator: Meiqi Liu, Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Long time well-posedness and wave turbulence limit for a quadratic non-lienar Schr{\"o}dinger equation with well prepared random initial data
item.description: arXiv:2609.28093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a long time well-posedness result for a quadratic non-linear Schr{\"o}dinger equation with random well prepared initial conditions in dimension d $\ge$ 1. In some regimes, we derive the Wave Kinetic equation associated with the equation in dimension d $\ge$ 5, almost up to the kinetic time to the power d/(d + 1). Our analysis relies on the ideas introduced by Deng and Hani.
item.dc:creator: Enguerrand Brun (UMPA-ENSL)

item.title: Convexity of inverse spectral Green kernels and nondegeneracy of Robin centers in convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2609.29288v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded convex domain, and let $A=-\Delta_D$ be the Dirichlet Laplacian. For every $s>0$ with $N>2s$, we prove that the Green-kernel transform $(x,y)\mapsto K_{s,\Omega}(x,y)^{-1/(N-2s)}$ extends continuously by zero to the diagonal and is jointly convex on $\Omega\times\Omega$. We prove that the regular part extends real analytically across the diagonal and that the associated Robin function is strictly convex and diverges to $+\infty$ at the boundary. Hence it has a unique critical point. If $\Omega$ is of class $C^{2,\vartheta}$, this point is nondegenerate for every $s>0$ with $N>2s$. Moreover, the Hessian of the Robin function is positive definite throughout $\Omega$ when $0<s<1$ or $N>3s$. The arguments combine convexity inequalities for Dirichlet heat kernels, a weighted boundary identity at fractional orders, and a finite-part transfer of Hessian positivity between spectral powers. In particular, the results apply to spectral fractional Dirichlet Laplacians and Navier polyharmonic operators.
item.dc:creator: Xiuda Liang, Wenjie Wang

item.title: Lamb dipole stability without sign condition
item.description: arXiv:2609.33578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the 2D incompressible Euler equations on the half-plane, we establish Lyapunov stability of the Lamb dipole without sign condition on the vorticity. The main challenge arises from growth of the $x_{2}$ weighted norm for mixed sign vorticities, whereas this norm is conserved and responsible for dipole stability in the single signed vorticity case. This difficulty is handled by a Lagrangian bootstrap argument, based on carefully dividing the solution into several pieces and analyzing interactions among them, with the most delicate interaction involving vorticity drifting to infinity in the vertical direction. We expect that the strategy developed here will provide a starting point for the stability analysis of more general vortex configurations, including interactions among multiple vortex dipoles and among multiple vortex rings in settings involving mixed-sign vorticity.
item.dc:creator: Ken Abe, Kyudong Choi, In-Jee Jeong, Guolin Qin

item.title: Uniqueness of one-phase cones with isolated singularity
item.description: arXiv:2609.35175v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove uniqueness of the blow-up at every singular point of the one-phase free boundary problem for which one blow-up has an isolated singularity. The result applies to Lipschitz stationary solutions and does not require any integrability assumption on the cone. In this sense, our result completes the picture for uniqueness of tangent cones at isolated singularities in the one-phase problem. Inspired by Simon's work in the minimal surface setting, we prove an infinite dimensional \L ojasiewicz inequality for the spherical Weiss' energy. This yields an epiperimetric inequality for non-minimizing solutions, which leads to the uniqueness result.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Carducci, Bozhidar Velichkov

item.title: Optimal multipolar Lp-Hardy inequalities: ground states, criticality and variational thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.00652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study ground states, criticality, and variational compactness for genuinely multipolar $L^p$-Hardy weights, $1<p<n$. A ground-state representation across the poles gives a complete criticality classification of the full potential and characterizes finite-energy attainment. Removing a geometric interaction term produces a variational problem governed by concentration at the poles and infinity. A strict concentration gap yields compactness, positive extremizers, and criticality of the optimal operator; for $p\ge2$, it is also necessary for attainment. In the subquadratic range, the optimal truncated coefficient is below one and attained throughout the full-potential critical set. For admissible parameters with $1<p<2$ and $(n-p)/p<s\le m(n-p)/p$, arbitrary fixed pole configurations exhibit negative directions, attained critical states, and coercive subcritical regimes outside this set along positive-weight paths towards the simplex vertices. A single-pole degeneration formula and continuity in the weights establish this coexistence. In the superquadratic range, an interaction threshold determines a non-attained infinity-concentration interval. Under strict separation from pole concentration, its endpoint is critical with infinite energy and a compact phase follows. We prove separation for every bipolar configuration and in several multipolar regimes, including a vertex neighborhood uniform in the exponent. Near parameters strictly inside the quadratic attained region, the optimal coefficient crosses one continuously through $p=2$. The proofs combine ground-state remainders, capacity, weighted compactness, and critical Hardy barriers.
item.dc:creator: Yongyang Jin, Shoufeng Shen, Li Tang

item.title: A constrained log-HLS inequality and its associated Wasserstein flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.05356v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a log-Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev (log-HLS) inequality under constraints and a naturally induced Wasserstein flow. The constrained log-HLS inequality is dual, in a variational sense, to the constrained Trudinger-Moser-Onofri-Aubin inequality. The corresponding gradient-flow formulation leads to a parabolic-elliptic Patlak-Keller-Segel (PKS) system whose global dynamics exhibit a dichotomy between global existence and finite-time blow-up depending on the initial mass. Remarkably, the constraint raises the critical mass threshold of the flow by a factor of two compared with the unconstrained setting. This provides a distinct mechanism for suppressing blow-up from those arising in related formulations of the PKS-system, where blow-up is mitigated through additional effects such as a forcing term, coupling with a fluid equation, or the ambient flow generated by harmonic perturbations of the Newtonian potential.
item.dc:creator: Monideep Ghosh, Debabrata Karmakar, Reetaj Sinha, Kartikey Verma

item.title: Fractional gradients and nonlocal PDEs in variable exponent spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.08253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a theory of distributional Riesz fractional gradients in variable exponent Lebesgue spaces and introduce the associated nonlocal Sobolev spaces. Moreover, Sobolev, Hardy, Morrey, and Trudinger-type inequalities are established, and a fractional fundamental theorem of calculus is derived. As an application, we study nonlinear variational problems with nonstandard growth and establish existence and Euler--Lagrange equations for minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Susana Moura, Cornelia Schneider

item.title: Uniqueness of Leray-Hopf weak solutions to the two-dimensional viscous Primitive Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.11339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Global existence of Leray-Hopf (type) weak solutions to the viscous primitive equations in two or three dimensions was established by Lions--Temam--Wang \cite{Lions1,Lions2,Lions3,Lions4} in the 1990s; however, the corresponding uniqueness, no matter in two or three dimensions, has been a long standing open problem since then. In this paper, we solve this open problem in the two-dimensional case. Precisely, we prove the uniqueness of Leray-Hopf weak solutions, with arbitrary $L^2$ initial data, to the viscous primitive equations in a periodic channel, subject to impermeability and stress-free boundary conditions on the solid boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Jinkai Li, Lintao Liu, Edriss S. Titi, Dong Wang

item.title: Nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in an exterior domain
item.description: arXiv:2610.11968v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the exact controllability of the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in the exterior $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Theta$ of a non-trapping obstacle $\Theta$, with internal controls supported outside a large ball, and the corresponding boundary control problem on $\Omega_0=B_{R_0}\setminus\Theta$ with Dirichlet controls acting only on the outer sphere $\partial B_{R_0}$. Using the local smoothing effect of Burq, G\'erard and Tzvetkov [9], we prove observability inequalities for the linear Schr\"odinger equation in the whole scale of Sobolev spaces $H^\sigma_D(\Omega)$, $\sigma\in[-2,2]$, associated with the Dirichlet Laplacian; they require only the non-trapping assumption (no star-shapedness of $\Theta$), and their proofs use no normal boundary traces. Combined with Strichartz-type estimates and a perturbation argument, this yields local exact controllability in $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and in $H^2(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, in dimensions two and three, around the zero solution and, for internal controls and under a unique continuation assumption, around nontrivial trajectories. The same method applies to the quintic equation, which is energy-critical in dimension three. Several open problems are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Roberto de A. Capistrano Filho (UFPE), Lionel Rosier (UCL), Bingyu Zhang (UC)

item.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13753v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. No smallness assumption is made, no zero mean condition is imposed, and the admissible data include all Schwartz functions. The proof uses the inverse scattering transform attached to the heat operator. It rests on three ingredients: an a priori bound for the scalar $\bar\partial$ problem which depends on the size of the scattering coefficient but not on its oscillating phase, a nonlinear Plancherel identity proved by analytic continuation from small data, and an estimate showing that the nonlinear part of the reconstruction is negligible on the propagation cones of free waves. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen

item.title: Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
item.description: arXiv:2312.00594v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $\lambda$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $\lambda$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.
item.dc:creator: Steven Flynn

item.title: Nonexistence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue near the round sphere in low dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2408.07823v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of minimizing the second conformal eigenvalue of the conformal Laplacian in a conformal class of metrics with renormalized volume. We prove, in dimensions $n\in\left\{3,\dotsc,10\right\}$, that a minimizer for this problem does not exist for metrics sufficiently close to the round metric on the sphere. This is in striking contrast with the situation in dimensions $n \ge 11$, where Ammann and Humbert obtained the existence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue on any smooth closed non-locally conformally flat manifold. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also obtain a lower bound on the energy of sign-changing solutions of the \nobreak Yamabe equation in dimensions 3, 4 and 5, which extends a result obtained by Weth in the case of the round sphere.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Premoselli, J\'er\^ome V\'etois

item.title: Stability of Minkowski-type inequalities in certain warped product spaces
item.description: arXiv:2505.06422v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper explores the stability of Minkowski-type inequalities for hypersurfaces in warped product spaces. We establish a stability estimate that bounds the norm of the traceless second fundamental form of the hypersurface in terms of the deficit in the Minkowski inequalities satisfied by the hypersurface. Additionally, we prove the stability of Minkowski inequalities in specific cases of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om Anti-de Sitter (RN-AdS) and Anti-de Sitter Schwarzschild (AdS-Schwarzschild) manifolds, which serve as examples of warped products. We also establish a new rigidity result for locally conformally flat manifolds to understand the stability of these inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Prachi Sahjwani

item.title: Quantitative homogenization of first-order ODEs
