item.description: arXiv:2508.17628v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the quantitative homogenization of first-order ODEs. For single-scale scalar ODEs, we obtain a sharp $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence rate and characterize the effective constant. In the multi-scale setting, our results match those of \cite{IM} for long times but improve the short-time error to $O(\varepsilon)$. We also obtain what appears to be the first uniform $O(\varepsilon)$ homogenization estimate for scalar ODEs with quasi-periodic fast dependence on the state variable. The scalar framework is further extended to higher dimensions under a bounded-mean-motion-type assumption. For weakly coupled systems with fast switching rates, we derive an explicit $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence rate that captures the initial layer. These results have applications to linear transport equations and broader connections to PDEs and gradient systems.
item.dc:creator: Panrui Ni

item.title: Bounded Toeplitz operators and unbounded projected multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2601.10711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a smooth, nonnegative radial symbol $g$ on $\mathbb C$ whose Toeplitz operator on Bargmann--Fock space is positive with singular values decaying faster than every exponential, while projected multiplication $f\mapsto P(gf)$ has no bounded extension from the ambient Gaussian $L^2$ space. All heat transforms of $g$ at positive times are Schwartz functions, and $g\in L^p(dA)$ for every $0<p<2$. We also construct smooth real symbols realizing every possible set of heat boundedness times. Any prescribed positive threshold may be included or excluded, with Schwartz transforms at every later time. All these symbols satisfy the coherent state domain condition, and all heat integrals converge absolutely.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: Wave scattering by a transversal defect in a discrete waveguide
item.description: arXiv:2602.10227v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study wave scattering by a finite transversal strip in a discrete square-lattice waveguide with Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on the strip and the waveguide walls. The setting is motivated as a discrete analogue of the classical continuous waveguide problem with a screen. The corresponding Wiener--Hopf formulation leads to an equation with a $4 \times 4$ matrix kernel, which reduces to a $2 \times 2$ matrix kernel under some symmetry assumptions. The prospects for factorising this kernel are discussed, but this approach is not pursued. Instead, an exact analytical solution is obtained using the pole removal technique. This contrasts with the continuous case, where only approximate solutions are currently available. The reflection and transmission coefficients resulting from an incident duct mode are computed with an accuracy up to $10^{-13}$, showing consistency with theoretical predictions from continuous waveguide theory. In particular, full reflection and zero transmission are recovered as the frequency approaches the cut-off value for the incident mode. Finally, the solution is validated against a numerical computation of the diffraction problem via the Boundary Algebraic Equations method with a tailored lattice Green's function.
item.dc:creator: Elena Medvedeva, Raphael Assier, Anastasia Kisil

item.title: Maximal growth of the Stein-Wainger oscillatory integral
item.description: arXiv:2603.23238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the optimal growth of the Stein--Wainger oscillatory integral for every Denjoy--Carleman class defined by a positive log-convex sequence. Quasianalyticity is equivalent to boundedness in $\lambda$ for every fixed phase in the class. In the nonquasianalytic case, an explicit formula in the defining sequence gives the optimal order, attained by a single phase for all sufficiently large frequencies. This yields sharp bounds for Gevrey classes, their logarithmic refinements, and classes beyond every Gevrey class. For general smooth phases the growth is $o(\log\lambda)$, and every prescribed $h(\lambda)\to\infty$ with $h(\lambda)=o(\log\lambda)$ is attained asymptotically along a sequence by one smooth phase. These results answer a question of Wang and Zhang motivated by endpoint eigenfunction restriction.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Zhang, Zhifei Zhu

item.title: The Korteweg-de Vries limit for the global dynamics of the Toda lattice
item.description: arXiv:2605.07532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It has been observed that the dynamics of the Toda lattice can be well described by solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation in the continuum limit. We show that, under the KdV scaling and a suitable translation, the solution of the Toda lattice with H^1 initial data converges to that of the KdV equation globally in time. Our proof relies on tools from harmonic analysis and also on the construction and the conservation of mass and energy of the Toda lattice, the latter of which are derived from the completely integrable structure of the Toda lattice. As a consequence, we obtain long-wave KdV limits for the Toda lattice.
item.dc:creator: Herbert Koch, Ruoyuan Liu

item.title: A Bernstein Theorem for the Self-Shrinking $J$-Equation and Some Generalizations
item.description: arXiv:2606.29546v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every entire smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution of the self-shrinking $J$-equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a quadratic polynomial. This removes the asymptotic lower bound assumption on the complex Hessian in \cite[Theorem 4]{HJ}. The result also recovers the corresponding real rigidity theorem in \cite[Theorem 1.1]{HOW} as a special case. More generally, our method applies to self-shrinking equations associated with a broad class of fully nonlinear elliptic operators satisfying suitable structural conditions, including the adjacent inverse complex Hessian quotient operators $-\sigma_{k-1}/\sigma_{k}$, $1\leq k\leq n$. For the remaining quotients $-\sigma_l/\sigma_k$ with $l<k-1$, we prove the same rigidity conclusion under the additional assumption that the solution is proper.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Pan, Wenlong Wang

item.title: Metric gradient flows and variational principles
item.description: arXiv:2608.01262v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Ekeland-type variational principles can be derived from steepest descent curves in metric spaces. From this, we relate the existence of the Calabi flow to the validity of the Ekeland variational principle for the $K$-energy on the space of K\"ahler potentials.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella

item.title: Rigidity and volume pinching for the sharp gradient estimate in positive Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.03739v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Colding established a sharp gradient estimate for the Green function on manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature, which was extended to positive Ricci curvature by Manea recently. We prove almost rigidity of such gradient estimates for positive Ricci curvature. We show that the average of the gradient deficit, namely $\fint (1-|\nabla b|^2)\,dV$, controls the volume deficit in an optimal quantitative manner; here $b$ is the distance-like function defined using the Green function. This implies a quantitative almost rigidity theorem for manifolds with $\ric\ge(n-1)g$ and a gap theorem for Einstein manifolds. We also prove a rigidity theorem for closed 4-dimensional Einstein manifolds by finding a new monotonicity formula.
item.dc:creator: Junyoung Kim, Jiewon Park

item.title: Exact Asymptotics for the 2D Euclidean Random Matching Problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.08717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the exact first-order asymptotics of the expected optimal cost in two-dimensional random bipartite matching, for every finite power cost $q \ge 1$, on the flat torus. In the endpoint case $q=1$, this answers a question by Talagrand, in the periodic case. The argument involves the closely related asymptotics of the energy of the solution of the $p$-Poisson equation with a regularized white-noise source. In the limit of vanishing regularization parameter, we identify this energy as the solution of a Variational Martingale Problem on a limiting Gaussian filtration, whose value is characterized by a parabolic Monge-Amp\`ere flow.
item.dc:creator: Victor Armegioiu, Michael Goldman, Francesco Grotto, Dario Trevisan

item.title: Bouncing-ball modes in ergodic billiards
item.description: arXiv:2609.36501v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for a horizontally stretched Bunimovich billiard, for almost every stretching parameter, there exists a sequence of eigenfunctions concentrating in the rectangular part. Thanks to the work of Markarian--Oliffson Kamphorst--Pinto de Carvalho, we know that for an open set of parameters such billiards are ergodic. The proof is a result of interaction with ChatGPT 6: we were curious if it could establish the existence of bouncing ball modes for Bunimovich or Sinai billiards. That was not successful until we suggested varying the wings. That produced an essentially complete argument for the existence of quasimodes. We then suggested using Hassell's parameter-variation argument which led to the result about eigenfunctions. The argument was then significantly simplified and clarified by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Li, Maciej Zworski

item.title: A geometric rigidity estimate for codimension-1 immersions into spheres
item.description: arXiv:2609.37665v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a quantitative stability estimate for codimension-one immersions into a round sphere. Let $(M,g)$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold and suppose that a prescribed shape operator is realised by a smooth isometric immersion $\theta:(M,g)\to\mathbb S^{n+1}$. We prove that, on every relatively compact strongly Lipschitz domain and for every $1<p<\infty$, any Sobolev immersion $\phi$ is close to $\theta$ modulo an ambient rotation, with the $W^{1,p}$-distances between both the immersions and their Gauss maps controlled by the $L^p$ stretching-plus-bending energies of $\phi$. No {\it a priori} bounds on the fundamental forms of $\phi$ are required. The proof proceeds by extending the immersions along normal geodesics and reducing the problem to an equidimensional geometric rigidity estimate on the sphere. A finite localisation and patching argument handles the possible non-injectivity of the normal extension of the reference immersion.
item.dc:creator: Siran Li, Isaac Newell

item.title: The isoperimetric problem for four-dimensional parallelohedra
item.description: arXiv:2610.01653v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The honeycomb and Kelvin problems ask how space can be partitioned into cells of equal volume with the least surface area. We resolve this question in four dimensions for convex bodies that tile space by translations, showing that the regular $24$-cell uniquely minimizes surface area at fixed volume. We develop a framework combining an exact deficit identity, valid in every dimension, with a descent argument. As a consequence, the regular $24$-cell also minimizes surface area among such tiles containing a fixed ball.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Novaga, Lark Song
